column3: The neutral word for any sit-down place to eat, small or big: 开餐馆 is to run one, 去餐馆吃饭 to eat out. 馆 ends many kinds of places, such as 宾馆 and 博物馆.
column6: Zhè jiā cānguǎn de cài hěn hǎochī.
column7: The food at this restaurant is very good.
column9: The neutral word for any sit-down place to eat, small or big: 開餐館 is to run one, 去餐館吃飯 to eat out. 館 ends many kinds of places, such as 賓館 and 博物館.

column3: A business and written word for the whole catering trade: 餐饮业, 餐饮服务. To talk about eating out in daily speech, people say 吃饭 or 餐馆 instead.
column4: 他在餐饮行业工作了十年。
column5: 他在餐飲行業工作了十年。
column6: Tā zài cānyǐn hángyè gōngzuò le shí nián.
column7: He has worked in the catering industry for ten years.
column9: A business and written word for the whole catering trade: 餐飲業, 餐飲服務. To talk about eating out in daily speech, people say 吃飯 or 餐館 instead.

column3: Used for eating habits in talk about health or custom: 饮食习惯, 健康饮食, 注意饮食. More formal than 吃, and it covers drinks too.
column4: 健康的饮食对身体很重要。
column5: 健康的飲食對身體很重要。
column6: Jiànkāng de yǐnshí duì shēntǐ hěn zhòngyào.
column7: A healthy diet is very important for the body.
column9: Used for eating habits in talk about health or custom: 飲食習慣, 健康飲食, 注意飲食. More formal than 吃, and it covers drinks too.

column3: On the mainland, "baijiu", the strong clear spirit distilled from grain, usually sorghum, drunk in small cups at banquets. It is 白 "white/clear" plus 酒 "alcohol". White wine is a different word, 白葡萄酒.
column6: Tā hē le yīdiǎn báijiǔ.
column7: He drank a little baijiu.
column9: On the mainland, "baijiu", the strong clear spirit distilled from grain, usually sorghum, drunk in small cups at banquets. It is 白 "white/clear" plus 酒 "alcohol". White wine is a different word, 白葡萄酒.

column3: For a glass say 一杯葡萄酒, for a bottle 一瓶. White wine is 白葡萄酒; in everyday speech red wine is usually just 红酒. 酒 alone covers any alcohol.
column6: Zhè píng pútáojiǔ shì Fǎguó de.
column7: This bottle of wine is from France.
column9: For a glass say 一杯葡萄酒, for a bottle 一瓶. White wine is 白葡萄酒; in everyday speech red wine is usually just 紅酒. 酒 alone covers any alcohol.

column3: A rude, spoken word for a heavy drinker; never say it of someone to their face. The 鬼 suffix also names people with a vice: 烟鬼 (chain smoker) and 赌鬼 (gambler).
column6: Tā bàba shì ge jiǔguǐ.
column7: His father is a drunkard.
column9: A rude, spoken word for a heavy drinker; never say it of someone to their face. The 鬼 suffix also names people with a vice: 煙鬼 (chain smoker) and 賭鬼 (gambler).

column3: Mostly the result of drinking: 喝醉 (drink until drunk), 醉了, 喝得大醉. It is also figurative, being intoxicated by something beautiful: 陶醉.
column6: Tā hē zuì le, hái zài chànggē.
column7: He is drunk and still singing.
column9: Mostly the result of drinking: 喝醉 (drink until drunk), 醉了, 喝得大醉. It is also figurative, being intoxicated by something beautiful: 陶醉.

column3: Any flat, round cake or bread: a pancake, flatbread or pastry. 煎饼 and 烙饼 are northern breakfast foods, and 饼 is the base of 饼干 and 月饼. Count a whole one with 张, a piece with 块.
column6: Zǎoshang wǒ chī le yī zhāng bǐng.
column7: This morning I ate a flatbread.
column9: Any flat, round cake or bread: a pancake, flatbread or pastry. 煎餅 and 烙餅 are northern breakfast foods, and 餅 is the base of 餅乾 and 月餅. Count a whole one with 張, a piece with 塊.

column3: Covers sweet cookies and salty crackers alike. Count one with 块 or 片, a packet with 包: 一包饼干.
column6: Háizi xǐhuan chī bǐnggān.
column7: Children like to eat cookies.
column9: Covers sweet cookies and salty crackers alike. Count one with 塊 or 片, a packet with 包: 一包餅乾.

column3: The round pastry of the Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节), often given as a boxed gift: 送月饼, 一盒月饼. Lotus seed paste and egg yolk are classic fillings.
column4: 中秋节我们一起吃月饼。
column5: 中秋節我們一起吃月餅。
column6: Zhōngqiūjié wǒmen yīqǐ chī yuèbǐng.
column7: At the Mid-Autumn Festival we eat mooncakes together.
column9: The round pastry of the Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋節), often given as a boxed gift: 送月餅, 一盒月餅. Lotus seed paste and egg yolk are classic fillings.

column3: A loan from Japanese, written with the characters Japanese uses for it, so neither character says anything about rice or fish here. Typical: 吃寿司, 寿司店, 一份寿司.
column6: Wǒmen zhōngwǔ qù chī shòusī ba.
column7: Let's go and eat sushi at noon.
column9: A loan from Japanese, written with the characters Japanese uses for it, so neither character says anything about rice or fish here. Typical: 吃壽司, 壽司店, 一份壽司.

column3: Above all Beijing roast duck (北京烤鸭), served with thin pancakes, scallions and sauce. 烤 also builds 烤鸡 and 烤肉, and 烤火 is to warm yourself by a fire.
column6: Lái Běijīng yīdìng yào chī kǎoyā.
column7: When you come to Beijing you must eat roast duck.
column9: Above all Beijing roast duck (北京烤鴨), served with thin pancakes, scallions and sauce. 烤 also builds 烤雞 and 烤肉, and 烤火 is to warm yourself by a fire.

column3: Barbecued or roast meat, and also the verb "to barbecue": 去野外烤肉 "go barbecue outdoors". In Korean restaurants 韩国烤肉 is Korean barbecue. In Taiwan 烤肉 is also the family barbecue held at the Mid-Autumn Festival. 烤 "roast" + 肉 "meat".
column4: 周末我们去吃韩国烤肉。
column5: 週末我們去吃韓國烤肉。
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù chī Hánguó kǎoròu.
column7: At the weekend we are going to eat Korean barbecue.
column9: Barbecued or roast meat, and also the verb "to barbecue": 去野外烤肉 "go barbecue outdoors". In Korean restaurants 韓國烤肉 is Korean barbecue. In Taiwan 烤肉 is also the family barbecue held at the Mid-Autumn Festival. 烤 "roast" + 肉 "meat".

column3: Rice with dishes in a partitioned box, sold at stations and on trains or ordered for the office at lunchtime. Count with 份: 一份盒饭, 订盒饭. The mainland word; in Taiwan the same boxed meal is 便当.
column4: 中午我们订了三份盒饭。
column5: 中午我們訂了三份盒飯。
column6: Zhōngwǔ wǒmen dìng le sān fèn héfàn.
column7: At noon we ordered three boxed meals.
column9: Rice with dishes in a partitioned box, sold at stations and on trains or ordered for the office at lunchtime. Count with 份: 一份盒飯, 訂盒飯. The mainland word; in Taiwan the same boxed meal is 便當.

column3: To taste, to try a food, and by extension to experience something. Doubled it means "have a taste": 尝尝 (the second one neutral), 尝一尝. The result form is 尝到 "to taste/experience": 尝到了甜头. It also appears in 尝试 "to attempt".
column6: Nǐ chángchang zhège cài.
column7: Try this dish.
column9: To taste, to try a food, and by extension to experience something. Doubled it means "have a taste": 嘗嘗 (the second one neutral), 嘗一嘗. The result form is 嘗到 "to taste/experience": 嘗到了甜頭. It also appears in 嘗試 "to attempt".

column3: More often figurative than about food: all the joys and sorrows of life, as in 尝遍了人生的酸甜苦辣. A set phrase of four flavors, with no particles inside it.
column6: Shēnghuó lǐ yǒu suāntiánkǔlà.
column7: Life has its sours, sweets, bitters and spices.
column9: More often figurative than about food: all the joys and sorrows of life, as in 嘗遍了人生的酸甜苦辣. A set phrase of four flavors, with no particles inside it.

column3: The ordinary word for an eating fork: 用叉子吃面. 叉 alone is a prong or pitchfork. 刀叉 is knife and fork, and chopsticks are 筷子.
column4: 我不会用筷子，我用叉子。
column5: 我不會用筷子，我用叉子。
column6: Wǒ bù huì yòng kuàizi, wǒ yòng chāzi.
column7: I can't use chopsticks, so I use a fork.
column9: The ordinary word for an eating fork: 用叉子吃麵. 叉 alone is a prong or pitchfork. 刀叉 is knife and fork, and chopsticks are 筷子.

column3: Alone it means a prong or pitchfork, and a cross mark: the X for a wrong answer is 叉, as in 打叉 and 画叉. As a verb it is to cross or intersect: 叉腰 is hands on hips, 交叉 to cross. An eating fork is 叉子.
column4: 老师在错题上画了一个叉。
column5: 老師在錯題上畫了一個叉。
column6: Lǎoshī zài cuòtí shàng huà le yī gè chā.
column7: The teacher drew a cross next to the wrong answer.
column9: Alone it means a prong or pitchfork, and a cross mark: the X for a wrong answer is 叉, as in 打叉 and 畫叉. As a verb it is to cross or intersect: 叉腰 is hands on hips, 交叉 to cross. An eating fork is 叉子.

column3: The general, slightly formal word: 新鲜蔬菜, 多吃蔬菜. In everyday speech 菜 or 青菜 is common, and 菜 by itself is also a dish, as in 点菜. 蔬菜 itself takes no measure word.
column6: Duō chī shūcài duì shēntǐ hǎo.
column7: Eating more vegetables is good for you.
column9: The general, slightly formal word: 新鮮蔬菜, 多吃蔬菜. In everyday speech 菜 or 青菜 is common, and 菜 by itself is also a dish, as in 點菜. 蔬菜 itself takes no measure word.

column3: Potato, literally "earth bean": 土 "earth, soil" + 豆 "bean". Typical dishes are 炒土豆丝 and 土豆炖牛肉. Watch the dialect difference: in Taiwan 土豆 means "peanut"; there a potato is 马铃薯. 豆 is a picture of a tall serving dish.
column4: 他今天晚上做了土豆牛肉。
column5: 他今天晚上做了土豆牛肉。
column6: Tā jīntiān wǎnshang zuò le tǔdòu niúròu.
column7: This evening he made beef with potatoes.
column9: Potato, literally "earth bean": 土 "earth, soil" + 豆 "bean". Typical dishes are 炒土豆絲 and 土豆燉牛肉. Watch the dialect difference: in Taiwan 土豆 means "peanut"; there a potato is 馬鈴薯. 豆 is a picture of a tall serving dish.

column3: Tomato, literally "western red persimmon". A staple of home cooking, with eggs in 西红柿炒鸡蛋 and in soups. In Taiwan the usual word is 番茄. The last character 柿 has 木 "tree" on the left and 市 on the right, which gives the sound shì.
column4: 西红柿炒鸡蛋是一道家常菜。
column5: 西紅柿炒雞蛋是一道家常菜。
column6: Xīhóngshì chǎo jīdàn shì yī dào jiācháng cài.
column7: Tomato with scrambled egg is a home-style dish.
column9: Tomato, literally "western red persimmon". A staple of home cooking, with eggs in 西紅柿炒雞蛋 and in soups. In Taiwan the usual word is 番茄. The last character 柿 has 木 "tree" on the left and 市 on the right, which gives the sound shì.

column3: Count with 串 for a bunch: 一串葡萄. It is the base of 葡萄干 (raisin) and 葡萄酒.
column6: Zhèxiē pútao yòu dà yòu tián.
column7: These grapes are big and sweet.
column9: Count with 串 for a bunch: 一串葡萄. It is the base of 葡萄乾 (raisin) and 葡萄酒.

column3: Peaches stand for long life, so an older person's birthday brings 寿桃, buns shaped like peaches. 桃 is the base of 桃花 and 桃树; the fruit in speech is often 桃子.
column4: 这棵树上的桃已经熟了。
column5: 這棵樹上的桃已經熟了。
column6: Zhè kē shù shàng de táo yǐjīng shú le.
column7: The peaches on this tree are already ripe.
column9: Peaches stand for long life, so an older person's birthday brings 壽桃, buns shaped like peaches. 桃 is the base of 桃花 and 桃樹; the fruit in speech is often 桃子.

column3: A folk belief says a pear must not be shared between two people, because 分梨 sounds like 分离, to part. In speech the fruit is often 梨子: 削梨 is to peel a pear.
column6: Zhège lí yòu cuì yòu tián.
column7: This pear is crisp and sweet.
column9: A folk belief says a pear must not be shared between two people, because 分梨 sounds like 分離, to part. In speech the fruit is often 梨子: 削梨 is to peel a pear.

column3: X + 品 names a kind of product: 豆制品, 水产品, 农产品. The bean products are tofu, soy milk, dried bean curd and the like.
column4: 豆制品里有很多蛋白质。
column5: 豆製品裡有很多蛋白質。
column6: Dòuzhìpǐn lǐ yǒu hěn duō dànbáizhì.
column7: Bean products contain a lot of protein.
column9: X + 品 names a kind of product: 豆製品, 水產品, 農產品. The bean products are tofu, soy milk, dried bean curd and the like.

column3: Fish, shrimp, crabs, shellfish and seaweed as goods for sale. A trade and market word: 水产品市场, 水产品加工. On a menu or in a shop, seafood is usually 海鲜.
column4: 这个市场有各种水产品。
column5: 這個市場有各種水產品。
column6: Zhège shìchǎng yǒu gèzhǒng shuǐchǎnpǐn.
column7: This market has all kinds of aquatic products.
column9: Fish, shrimp, crabs, shellfish and seaweed as goods for sale. A trade and market word: 水產品市場, 水產品加工. On a menu or in a shop, seafood is usually 海鮮.

column3: A market and policy word for farm output: 农产品价格, 农产品出口, 绿色农产品. It is one of the X + 品 words, like 水产品; 产品 alone is any product.
column4: 农产品的价格最近上涨了。
column5: 農產品的價格最近上漲了。
column6: Nóngchǎnpǐn de jiàgé zuìjìn shàngzhǎng le.
column7: The price of farm produce has risen recently.
column9: A market and policy word for farm output: 農產品價格, 農產品出口, 綠色農產品. It is one of the X + 品 words, like 水產品; 產品 alone is any product.

column3: Count with 根: 一根香肠. Grilled sausages are a street and night-market snack, and 腊肠 is Chinese cured sausage.
column6: Zǎofàn tā chī le liǎng gēn xiāngcháng.
column7: For breakfast he ate two sausages.
column9: Count with 根: 一根香腸. Grilled sausages are a street and night-market snack, and 臘腸 is Chinese cured sausage.

column3: Also the sliced ham in a sandwich: 火腿三明治. 金华火腿 is a famous Chinese cured ham. 腿 alone is a leg, including an animal's, as in 鸡腿.
column6: Wǒ yào yī gè huǒtuǐ sānmíngzhì.
column7: I'd like a ham sandwich.
column9: Also the sliced ham in a sandwich: 火腿三明治. 金華火腿 is a famous Chinese cured ham. 腿 alone is a leg, including an animal's, as in 雞腿.

column3: Usually a verb in a clause: 今年丰收了. Also figurative for big gains: 大丰收, 喜获丰收, and 丰收年 for a bumper year.
column6: Jīnnián de píngguǒ fēngshōu le.
column7: There was a bumper apple harvest this year.
column9: Usually a verb in a clause: 今年豐收了. Also figurative for big gains: 大豐收, 喜獲豐收, and 豐收年 for a bumper year.

column3: Crisp food: 又香又脆. It also describes a clear, ringing sound (清脆) and things that break easily (脆弱). In 干脆, 脆 means clean and neat, and the word means simply or straight out.
column4: 炸鸡外面很脆，里面很嫩。
column5: 炸雞外面很脆，裡面很嫩。
column6: Zhàjī wàimiàn hěn cuì, lǐmiàn hěn nèn.
column7: The fried chicken is crispy outside and tender inside.
column9: Crisp food: 又香又脆. It also describes a clear, ringing sound (清脆) and things that break easily (脆弱). In 乾脆, 脆 means clean and neat, and the word means simply or straight out.

column3: A verb for freezing and for feeling very cold: 冻死了, 冻手. In a result clause, 冻得发抖 is to shiver with cold. It also means jelly, as in 果冻. Frozen things are 冰冻 or 冷冻.
column4: 外面太冷了，我冻得发抖。
column5: 外面太冷了，我凍得發抖。
column6: Wàimiàn tài lěng le, wǒ dòng de fādǒu.
column7: It is so cold outside that I am shivering.
column9: A verb for freezing and for feeling very cold: 凍死了, 凍手. In a result clause, 凍得發抖 is to shiver with cold. It also means jelly, as in 果凍. Frozen things are 冰凍 or 冷凍.

column3: Mostly northern and colloquial on its own: 进屋, 回屋, 屋里. Elsewhere people say 屋子 or 房间. It is common in compounds: 房屋, 屋顶 (roof).
column6: Nǐ jìn wū zuò ba.
column7: Come in and sit down.
column9: Mostly northern and colloquial on its own: 進屋, 回屋, 屋裡. Elsewhere people say 屋子 or 房間. It is common in compounds: 房屋, 屋頂 (roof).

column3: The bedroom of a home: 在卧室睡觉. 房间 is any room, and 卧房 also means bedroom. 室 ends many rooms: 浴室, 教室, 办公室.
column6: Wǒ de wòshì zài èr lóu.
column7: My bedroom is on the second floor.
column9: The bedroom of a home: 在臥室睡覺. 房間 is any room, and 臥房 also means bedroom. 室 ends many rooms: 浴室, 教室, 辦公室.

column3: Where guests are received and the family sits and watches TV: 在客厅看电视. Apartments are described by their rooms, such as 两室一厅.
column6: Háizimen zài kètīng kàn diànshì.
column7: The children are watching TV in the living room.
column9: Where guests are received and the family sits and watches TV: 在客廳看電視. Apartments are described by their rooms, such as 兩室一廳.

column3: 厨 is also in 厨师, a cook or chef. 房 names rooms in 书房 (study) and 房间 (room), and 做饭 is the verb that goes with this room.
column6: Māma zhèngzài chúfáng zuò fàn.
column7: Mom is cooking in the kitchen.
column9: 廚 is also in 廚師, a cook or chef. 房 names rooms in 書房 (study) and 房間 (room), and 做飯 is the verb that goes with this room.

column3: The big open room at the entrance of a hotel, station, airport or office building: 在大厅等. It is not 客厅, the living room of a home.
column6: Wǒmen zài jiǔdiàn dàtīng děng nǐ.
column7: We'll wait for you in the hotel lobby.
column9: The big open room at the entrance of a hotel, station, airport or office building: 在大廳等. It is not 客廳, the living room of a home.

column3: Mostly in compounds for a large public room or a room of the home: 客厅, 餐厅 (dining hall, restaurant), 大厅. In apartment ads, 两室一厅 is two bedrooms and a living room. It is also a government office level under a province: 教育厅.
column6: Zhè tào fángzi yǒu liǎng shì yī tīng.
column7: This apartment has two bedrooms and a living room.
column9: Mostly in compounds for a large public room or a room of the home: 客廳, 餐廳 (dining hall, restaurant), 大廳. In apartment ads, 兩室一廳 is two bedrooms and a living room. It is also a government office level under a province: 教育廳.

column3: The surface of a room's wall: 墙壁上挂着画. Somewhat written; in speech people say 墙 alone, counted with 面 or 堵: 一堵墙.
column6: Qiángbì shàng guà zhe yī fú huà.
column7: A painting hangs on the wall.
column9: The surface of a room's wall: 牆壁上掛著畫. Somewhat written; in speech people say 牆 alone, counted with 面 or 堵: 一堵牆.

column3: Works as a noun for the next-door home or neighbor and as a modifier: 隔壁邻居, 住在隔壁, 隔壁的房间. 隔 on its own can also mean at an interval, as in 隔天.
column6: Gébì zhù zhe yī wèi lǎorén.
column7: An old person lives next door.
column9: Works as a noun for the next-door home or neighbor and as a modifier: 隔壁鄰居, 住在隔壁, 隔壁的房間. 隔 on its own can also mean at an interval, as in 隔天.

column3: Typical verbs: 拉窗帘 to draw the curtains, 拉开 to open them, 挂窗帘 to hang them. 帘 also hangs in 门帘, a door curtain.
column6: Qǐng bǎ chuānglián lā kāi.
column7: Please open the curtains.
column9: Typical verbs: 拉窗簾 to draw the curtains, 拉開 to open them, 掛窗簾 to hang them. 簾 also hangs in 門簾, a door curtain.

column3: Any furniture with doors or drawers for storing things: 衣柜 is a wardrobe, 鞋柜 a shoe cabinet. The same 柜 forms 柜台, a counter. Most furniture takes the suffix 子: 桌子, 椅子, 柜子.
column6: Yīfu zài guìzi lǐ.
column7: The clothes are in the cupboard.
column9: Any furniture with doors or drawers for storing things: 衣櫃 is a wardrobe, 鞋櫃 a shoe cabinet. The same 櫃 forms 櫃檯, a counter. Most furniture takes the suffix 子: 桌子, 椅子, 櫃子.

column3: Usually has doors; open shelves are 书架. 书 + furniture gives 书桌 (desk) and 书架 as well.
column6: Shūguì lǐ yǒu hěn duō Zhōngwén shū.
column7: There are many Chinese books in the bookcase.
column9: Usually has doors; open shelves are 書架. 書 + furniture gives 書桌 (desk) and 書架 as well.

column3: A desk for reading and writing: 坐在书桌前, 整理书桌. A plain 桌子 is a table.
column6: Tā de shūzhuō zǒngshì hěn luàn.
column7: His desk is always messy.
column9: A desk for reading and writing: 坐在書桌前, 整理書桌. A plain 桌子 is a table.

column3: The material: 玻璃窗, 玻璃杯. A single pane or piece is 块玻璃. Eyeglasses are not 玻璃 but 眼镜.
column6: Chuānghu de bōli suì le.
column7: The glass of the window is broken.
column9: The material: 玻璃窗, 玻璃杯. A single pane or piece is 塊玻璃. Eyeglasses are not 玻璃 but 眼鏡.

column3: A basin for washing the face and hands, often plastic or enamel, at home or in a dormitory: 一个脸盆. The verb for washing your face is 洗脸.
column6: Tā bǎ shuǐ dào jìn liǎnpén lǐ.
column7: She poured the water into the basin.
column9: A basin for washing the face and hands, often plastic or enamel, at home or in a dormitory: 一個臉盆. The verb for washing your face is 洗臉.

column3: A small pool or pond, dug out or built to hold water: 小池子, 池子里有鱼. 池 alone shows up in 游泳池, 水池 and 电池.
column6: Yuànzi lǐ yǒu yī gè xiǎo chízi.
column7: There is a small pond in the yard.
column9: A small pool or pond, dug out or built to hold water: 小池子, 池子裡有魚. 池 alone shows up in 游泳池, 水池 and 電池.

column3: Pots, pans and woks: 炒锅 (wok), 火锅 (hotpot), and 一口锅 with the measure word 口. Figuratively 背锅 is to take the blame. The sense of blame is a clipping of 黑锅.
column6: Guō lǐ de tāng kuài kāi le.
column7: The soup in the pot is about to boil.
column9: Pots, pans and woks: 炒鍋 (wok), 火鍋 (hotpot), and 一口鍋 with the measure word 口. Figuratively 背鍋 is to take the blame. The sense of blame is a clipping of 黑鍋.

column3: A basic kitchen item in nearly every home: 用电饭锅煮饭. 电 starts many appliances, such as 电视 and 电冰箱.
column6: Wǒ yòng diànfànguō zhǔ fàn.
column7: I cook rice in a rice cooker.
column9: A basic kitchen item in nearly every home: 用電飯鍋煮飯. 電 starts many appliances, such as 電視 and 電冰箱.

column3: Mostly a measure word for boxed things: 一盒巧克力, 一盒牛奶. The thing itself is 盒子, and 盒 also ends words such as 铅笔盒 and 饭盒.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī hé qiǎokèlì.
column7: I bought a box of chocolates.
column9: Mostly a measure word for boxed things: 一盒巧克力, 一盒牛奶. The thing itself is 盒子, and 盒 also ends words such as 鉛筆盒 and 飯盒.

column3: The everyday noun for a small box that closes: 铅笔盒, 礼品盒, 打开盒子. A bigger box for storage or luggage is 箱子.
column6: Hézi lǐ shì shénme?
column7: What is in the box?
column9: The everyday noun for a small box that closes: 鉛筆盒, 禮品盒, 打開盒子. A bigger box for storage or luggage is 箱子.

column3: A basin, bowl or pot, and a measure word for what sits in one: 一盆花, 一盆水. Related words are 花盆 (flower pot), 脸盆 and 盆地 (a land basin).
column6: Yángtái shàng yǒu yī pén huā.
column7: There is a pot of flowers on the balcony.
column9: A basin, bowl or pot, and a measure word for what sits in one: 一盆花, 一盆水. Related words are 花盆 (flower pot), 臉盆 and 盆地 (a land basin).

column3: Strike one with 划: 划火柴. Count with 根, or 盒 for a box. 柴 alone is firewood, so it is literally fire sticks. A lighter is 打火机.
column6: Wǒ zhǎo bu dào huǒchái le.
column7: I can't find the matches.
column9: Strike one with 劃: 劃火柴. Count with 根, or 盒 for a box. 柴 alone is firewood, so it is literally fire sticks. A lighter is 打火機.

column3: Coal: 烧煤, 一吨煤, 煤矿. Words with it are often about heating and energy: 煤炭 is coal as fuel, 煤气 is gas for cooking and heating.
column4: 这个城市冬天用煤取暖。
column5: 這個城市冬天用煤取暖。
column6: Zhège chéngshì dōngtiān yòng méi qǔnuǎn.
column7: This city uses coal for heating in winter.
column9: Coal: 燒煤, 一噸煤, 煤礦. Words with it are often about heating and energy: 煤炭 is coal as fuel, 煤氣 is gas for cooking and heating.

column3: Gas used for cooking and heating at home, originally made from coal: 煤气灶 "gas stove", 煤气罐 "gas cylinder", 关煤气 "turn off the gas". The word can also mean carbon monoxide: 煤气中毒. In Taiwan household gas is called 瓦斯. 煤 "coal" + 气 "gas, air".
column6: Zuò wán fàn yào guān méiqì.
column7: After cooking you must turn off the gas.
column9: Gas used for cooking and heating at home, originally made from coal: 煤氣灶 "gas stove", 煤氣罐 "gas cylinder", 關煤氣 "turn off the gas". The word can also mean carbon monoxide: 煤氣中毒. In Taiwan household gas is called 瓦斯. 煤 "coal" + 氣 "gas, air".

column3: Count with 把: 一把剪刀. 剪 is the verb for cutting with scissors, as in 剪头发 and 剪纸. Other blades: 菜刀, 小刀. 剪 also means to edit video or audio.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī bǎ jiǎndāo.
column7: Please give me a pair of scissors.
column9: Count with 把: 一把剪刀. 剪 is the verb for cutting with scissors, as in 剪頭髮 and 剪紙. Other blades: 菜刀, 小刀. 剪 also means to edit video or audio.

column3: The spoken, informal word; 剪刀 is the standard one and the one you read on packaging. The suffix 子 is typical of everyday nouns, and the counter is 把: 一把剪子.
column6: Jiǎnzi zài chōuti lǐ.
column7: The scissors are in the drawer.
column9: The spoken, informal word; 剪刀 is the standard one and the one you read on packaging. The suffix 子 is typical of everyday nouns, and the counter is 把: 一把剪子.

column3: The thing cut comes right after it: 剪头发, 剪指甲, 剪纸, 剪布. It is also used for video work: 剪视频 and the noun 剪辑 (an edit).
column6: Wǒ xiǎng qù jiǎn tóufa.
column7: I want to go and get a haircut.
column9: The thing cut comes right after it: 剪頭髮, 剪指甲, 剪紙, 剪布. It is also used for video work: 剪視頻 and the noun 剪輯 (an edit).

column3: Liquid glue, in a bottle: 一瓶胶水. The usual verbs are 用 and 粘 or 贴. A glue stick is 胶棒; tape is 胶带. The 胶 is also in 橡胶, rubber.
column4: 用胶水把纸贴在本子上。
column5: 用膠水把紙貼在本子上。
column6: Yòng jiāoshuǐ bǎ zhǐ tiē zài běnzi shàng.
column7: Stick the paper onto the notebook with glue.
column9: Liquid glue, in a bottle: 一瓶膠水. The usual verbs are 用 and 粘 or 貼. A glue stick is 膠棒; tape is 膠帶. The 膠 is also in 橡膠, rubber.

column3: Counted by the roll: 一卷胶带. Clear tape is 透明胶带 and packing tape 封箱胶带. The 带 is a band or strip, as in 领带 and 皮带.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī juǎn jiāodài.
column7: Please give me a roll of tape.
column9: Counted by the roll: 一卷膠帶. Clear tape is 透明膠帶 and packing tape 封箱膠帶. The 帶 is a band or strip, as in 領帶 and 皮帶.

column3: The ink pen, counted with 支. 钢笔字 means writing done with one, usually neat. A ballpoint is 圆珠笔 and a pencil 铅笔: 笔 ends the name of every writing tool.
column6: Yéye xǐhuan yòng gāngbǐ xiězì.
column7: Grandfather likes to write with a fountain pen.
column9: The ink pen, counted with 支. 鋼筆字 means writing done with one, usually neat. A ballpoint is 圓珠筆 and a pencil 鉛筆: 筆 ends the name of every writing tool.

column3: The brush for calligraphy and ink painting, counted with 支. 毛笔字 is brush writing; you 练毛笔字 to practice it. Ordinary pens are set against it as 硬笔.
column6: Tā měitiān yòng máobǐ liànzì.
column7: He practices calligraphy with a brush every day.
column9: The brush for calligraphy and ink painting, counted with 支. 毛筆字 is brush writing; you 練毛筆字 to practice it. Ordinary pens are set against it as 硬筆.

column3: Both the lock (一把锁) and the verb: 锁门, 锁好, 锁上. Added to a place or a thing it means to shut something inside: 锁在家里. Also 锁屏 for locking a phone screen.
column6: Chūmén qián bié wàng le suǒ mén.
column7: Don't forget to lock the door before you go out.
column9: Both the lock (一把鎖) and the verb: 鎖門, 鎖好, 鎖上. Added to a place or a thing it means to shut something inside: 鎖在家裡. Also 鎖屏 for locking a phone screen.

column3: A hand fan, counted with 把 and used with 摇 or 拿. An electric fan is never 扇子 but 风扇 or 电风扇; a folding fan is 折扇.
column6: Xiàtiān tā ná zhe yī bǎ shànzi.
column7: In summer she holds a fan.
column9: A hand fan, counted with 把 and used with 搖 or 拿. An electric fan is never 扇子 but 風扇 or 電風扇; a folding fan is 折扇.

column3: Measure word for things that swing or slide on a frame: 一扇门, 一扇窗, 一扇屏风. A building is 栋 and a room 间, never 扇.
column6: Nà shàn chuānghu kāi zhe.
column7: That window is open.
column9: Measure word for things that swing or slide on a frame: 一扇門, 一扇窗, 一扇屏風. A building is 棟 and a room 間, never 扇.

column3: A verb that takes an object: 扇风, 扇火, 扇扇子. 用手扇 is the everyday way to cool yourself. 扇耳光 is a slap on the face.
column6: Tiān tài rè le, tā yòng shǒu shān fēng.
column7: It was so hot that he fanned himself with his hand.
column9: A verb that takes an object: 扇風, 扇火, 扇扇子. 用手扇 is the everyday way to cool yourself. 扇耳光 is a slap on the face.

column3: Cylindrical cells are counted with 节: 一节电池. You 换电池, and 没电了 says it is out of power. 电 opens a large family: 电话, 电脑, 电视, 电梯.
column6: Shǒujī diànchí méi diàn le.
column7: The phone battery is dead.
column9: Cylindrical cells are counted with 節: 一節電池. You 換電池, and 沒電了 says it is out of power. 電 opens a large family: 電話, 電腦, 電視, 電梯.

column3: Mostly met in compounds: 门铃 (doorbell), 闹铃 (alarm), 铃声. Alone it is the bell you ring or hear: 按铃, 铃响了. Counted with 个.
column4: 铃响了，同学们回到教室。
column5: 鈴響了，同學們回到教室。
column6: Líng xiǎng le, tóngxuémen huídào jiàoshì.
column7: The bell rang and the students went back to the classroom.
column9: Mostly met in compounds: 門鈴 (doorbell), 鬧鈴 (alarm), 鈴聲. Alone it is the bell you ring or hear: 按鈴, 鈴響了. Counted with 個.

column3: Ringtone (手机铃声) and the sound of a bell or doorbell, with the verb 响. You 设置 or 换 a ringtone. 声 added to a thing names its sound: 脚步声, 笑声, 歌声.
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī língshēng tài chǎo le.
column7: My phone's ringtone is too loud.
column9: Ringtone (手機鈴聲) and the sound of a bell or doorbell, with the verb 響. You 設置 or 換 a ringtone. 聲 added to a thing names its sound: 腳步聲, 笑聲, 歌聲.

column3: A suit, jacket and pants together: 一套西装; the jacket alone is 西装外套. 西服 is a near-synonym, a little more formal. 西 marks Western-style things: 西餐, 西药, 西医.
column6: Tā chuān zhe xīzhuāng qù miànshì.
column7: He went to the interview in a suit.
column9: A suit, jacket and pants together: 一套西裝; the jacket alone is 西裝外套. 西服 is a near-synonym, a little more formal. 西 marks Western-style things: 西餐, 西藥, 西醫.

column3: Counted with 条, as for all pants. 牛仔 gives the whole denim family: 牛仔裙, 牛仔外套, 牛仔布. The usual verb is 穿.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī tiáo niúzǎikù.
column7: I want to buy a pair of jeans.
column9: Counted with 條, as for all pants. 牛仔 gives the whole denim family: 牛仔裙, 牛仔外套, 牛仔布. The usual verb is 穿.

column3: The padded winter coat, counted with 件. 羽绒 alone is down (羽绒被 is a down comforter). 服 ends many clothing words: 校服, 制服, 西服, 衣服.
column6: Dōngtiān wǒ chuān yǔróngfú.
column7: In winter I wear a down jacket.
column9: The padded winter coat, counted with 件. 羽絨 alone is down (羽絨被 is a down comforter). 服 ends many clothing words: 校服, 制服, 西服, 衣服.

column3: Counted with 双: 一双高跟鞋; you 穿 them, and 踩 is to walk in them. Flat shoes are 平底鞋. 鞋 ends the whole family: 皮鞋, 运动鞋, 拖鞋, 凉鞋.
column6: Tā bù xíguàn chuān gāogēnxié.
column7: She is not used to wearing high heels.
column9: Counted with 雙: 一雙高跟鞋; you 穿 them, and 踩 is to walk in them. Flat shoes are 平底鞋. 鞋 ends the whole family: 皮鞋, 運動鞋, 拖鞋, 涼鞋.

column3: The formal shoe, set against 运动鞋. You 穿 them and 擦 them. 皮 plus a thing names leather goods: 皮包, 皮带, 皮衣, 皮沙发.
column6: Bàba měitiān zǎoshang cā píxié.
column7: Dad polishes his leather shoes every morning.
column9: The formal shoe, set against 運動鞋. You 穿 them and 擦 them. 皮 plus a thing names leather goods: 皮包, 皮帶, 皮衣, 皮沙發.

column3: The verbs are 打 and 系 (to tie it); counted with 条. A bow tie is 领结. 领 is also in 衣领 and 领导. A scholar traces 领 from neck and collar, through taking someone by the neck, to leading.
column4: 他打了一条蓝色的领带。
column5: 他打了一條藍色的領帶。
column6: Tā dǎ le yī tiáo lánsè de lǐngdài.
column7: He wore a blue tie.
column9: The verbs are 打 and 繫 (to tie it); counted with 條. A bow tie is 領結. 領 is also in 衣領 and 領導. A scholar traces 領 from neck and collar, through taking someone by the neck, to leading.

column3: You 披 a coat or scarf over your shoulders without putting your arms in: 披着外套, 披上, and the noun 披肩 (shawl). 披头发 or 披散 describes hair worn loose.
column6: Tā jiān shàng pī zhe yī tiáo wéijīn.
column7: She has a scarf draped over her shoulders.
column9: You 披 a coat or scarf over your shoulders without putting your arms in: 披著外套, 披上, and the noun 披肩 (shawl). 披頭髮 or 披散 describes hair worn loose.

column3: Counted with 个; a two-strap backpack is 双肩包 and a school bag 书包. 背包 also modifies other words: 背包客 is a backpacker and 背包旅行 is backpack travel.
column6: Wǒ de bēibāo lǐ yǒu yī píng shuǐ.
column7: There is a bottle of water in my backpack.
column9: Counted with 個; a two-strap backpack is 雙肩包 and a school bag 書包. 背包 also modifies other words: 背包客 is a backpacker and 背包旅行 is backpack travel.

column3: Often followed by 得 or 成: 打扮得很漂亮, 打扮成公主. It covers clothes, hair and makeup together, the effort of looking good. 精心打扮 is dressing up carefully. 扮 alone plays a role, as in 扮演.
column6: Tā jīntiān dǎban de hěn piàoliang.
column7: She is dressed up beautifully today.
column9: Often followed by 得 or 成: 打扮得很漂亮, 打扮成公主. It covers clothes, hair and makeup together, the effort of looking good. 精心打扮 is dressing up carefully. 扮 alone plays a role, as in 扮演.

column3: Blunt for a person; for things 难看 is milder. It also stands in 丑闻 (scandal) and 出丑 (make a fool of yourself).
column6: Zhè zhī gǒu kàn qǐlái hěn chǒu.
column7: This dog looks ugly.
column9: Blunt for a person; for things 難看 is milder. It also stands in 醜聞 (scandal) and 出醜 (make a fool of yourself).

column3: Praise for a smile, a voice, eyes or scenery. A verb plus 人 gives an adjective for what affects people: 迷人, 感人, 动人, 吓人, 烦人. The 迷 is also in 迷路 (get lost) and 球迷 (a sports fan).
column6: Tā de xiàoróng hěn mírén.
column7: Her smile is very charming.
column9: Praise for a smile, a voice, eyes or scenery. A verb plus 人 gives an adjective for what affects people: 迷人, 感人, 動人, 嚇人, 煩人. The 迷 is also in 迷路 (get lost) and 球迷 (a sports fan).

column3: Spoken, about how a person or thing looks: 变了模样, 长得什么模样. After an age it means about: 三十岁模样. 样子 is the more common everyday word.
column4: 孩子们长大了，都变了模样。
column5: 孩子們長大了，都變了模樣。
column6: Háizimen zhǎngdà le, dōu biàn le múyàng.
column7: The children have grown up and all look different.
column9: Spoken, about how a person or thing looks: 變了模樣, 長得什麼模樣. After an age it means about: 三十歲模樣. 樣子 is the more common everyday word.

column3: Formal. For a person it is the face and features; for a city, a village or a company it is the overall look: 城市面貌, 精神面貌 (mental outlook), 面貌一新. In talk about a face, 长相 is the plain word.
column4: 这座城市的面貌发生了很大变化。
column5: 這座城市的面貌發生了很大變化。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì de miànmào fāshēng le hěn dà biànhuà.
column7: The look of this city has changed greatly.
column9: Formal. For a person it is the face and features; for a city, a village or a company it is the overall look: 城市面貌, 精神面貌 (mental outlook), 面貌一新. In talk about a face, 長相 is the plain word.

column3: Praise for manner and bearing, mostly of a man, not for looks: 很有风度, 风度翩翩. 风 here is style, not wind, as in 作风 and 风格.
column4: 他很有风度，大家都喜欢他。
column5: 他很有風度，大家都喜歡他。
column6: Tā hěn yǒu fēngdù, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan tā.
column7: He has great poise and everybody likes him.
column9: Praise for manner and bearing, mostly of a man, not for looks: 很有風度, 風度翩翩. 風 here is style, not wind, as in 作風 and 風格.

column3: The look on a face that shows the state of mind, more written than 表情: 神情紧张, 神情严肃. Unlike 表情 it covers the eyes and the whole bearing.
column6: Tā de shénqíng hěn jǐnzhāng.
column7: She looks very tense.
column9: The look on a face that shows the state of mind, more written than 表情: 神情緊張, 神情嚴肅. Unlike 表情 it covers the eyes and the whole bearing.

column3: Both complexion (health) and mood. 脸色不好 can mean she looks pale or that she is in a bad mood; context decides. 看脸色 is reading someone's mood, 给他脸色看 a cold look.
column4: 你的脸色不太好，是不是生病了？
column5: 你的臉色不太好，是不是生病了？
column6: Nǐ de liǎnsè bù tài hǎo, shì bu shì shēngbìng le?
column7: You don't look well. Are you sick?
column9: Both complexion (health) and mood. 臉色不好 can mean she looks pale or that she is in a bad mood; context decides. 看臉色 is reading someone's mood, 給他臉色看 a cold look.

column3: The spoken word for mind or thinking power: 动脑子, 脑子好, 没脑子, 脑子里想着. 脑袋 is the colloquial head. 电脑, computer, is literally an electric brain.
column6: Nǐ dòngdong nǎozi xiǎng yī xiǎng.
column7: Use your head and think about it.
column9: The spoken word for mind or thinking power: 動腦子, 腦子好, 沒腦子, 腦子裡想著. 腦袋 is the colloquial head. 電腦, computer, is literally an electric brain.

column3: The brain as an organ, in science and health talk: 大脑发育, 保护大脑. In speech people say 脑子 for the thinking mind.
column6: Shuìmián duì dànǎo hěn zhòngyào.
column7: Sleep is important for the brain.
column9: The brain as an organ, in science and health talk: 大腦發育, 保護大腦. In speech people say 腦子 for the thinking mind.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 大肠, 小肠, 肠胃 (the digestive tract, as in 肠胃不好), 肠炎, and sausage: 香肠, 腊肠. The idiom 肠子都悔青了 means to regret something bitterly.
column4: 他的肠有点问题，要做检查。
column5: 他的腸有點問題，要做檢查。
column6: Tā de cháng yǒudiǎn wèntí, yào zuò jiǎnchá.
column7: There is something wrong with his intestines, so he needs tests.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 大腸, 小腸, 腸胃 (the digestive tract, as in 腸胃不好), 腸炎, and sausage: 香腸, 臘腸. The idiom 腸子都悔青了 means to regret something bitterly.

column3: Far more often courage than the organ: 胆大, 胆小, 大胆, 胆小鬼 (coward). The spoken form is 胆子: 有胆子, 没胆子. The organ is 胆囊 in medical talk.
column4: 他胆很小，不敢一个人睡。
column5: 他膽很小，不敢一個人睡。
column6: Tā dǎn hěn xiǎo, bù gǎn yī gè rén shuì.
column7: He is timid and does not dare sleep alone.
column9: Far more often courage than the organ: 膽大, 膽小, 大膽, 膽小鬼 (coward). The spoken form is 膽子: 有膽子, 沒膽子. The organ is 膽囊 in medical talk.

column3: The organ itself: 胃疼 points inside, while 肚子疼 is the ordinary word for a bellyache. 胃口 is appetite: 胃口好. 胃病 is stomach trouble. The 田 inside is not a field: an older form had a part like 米 inside, representing grains within the stomach, and the top was later simplified to the unrelated 田.
column6: Wǒ de wèi yǒudiǎnr téng.
column7: My stomach hurts a little.
column9: The organ itself: 胃疼 points inside, while 肚子疼 is the ordinary word for a bellyache. 胃口 is appetite: 胃口好. 胃病 is stomach trouble. The 田 inside is not a field: an older form had a part like 米 inside, representing grains within the stomach, and the top was later simplified to the unrelated 田.

column3: The everyday word for the body part is 肩膀; 肩 alone stays in set phrases: 肩上, 双肩, 披肩. As a verb it means to carry a duty: 肩负责任.
column6: Tā jiān shàng bēi zhe yī gè dà bāo.
column7: He carries a big bag on his shoulder.
column9: The everyday word for the body part is 肩膀; 肩 alone stays in set phrases: 肩上, 雙肩, 披肩. As a verb it means to carry a duty: 肩負責任.

column3: Muscle of the body: 练肌肉, 肌肉发达, 肌肉酸痛, 肌肉拉伤 (a pulled muscle). Meat for food is 肉 alone.
column4: 他每天去健身房练肌肉。
column5: 他每天去健身房練肌肉。
column6: Tā měitiān qù jiànshēnfáng liàn jīròu.
column7: He goes to the gym every day to build muscle.
column9: Muscle of the body: 練肌肉, 肌肉發達, 肌肉酸痛, 肌肉拉傷 (a pulled muscle). Meat for food is 肉 alone.

column3: A person's skin: 皮肤白, 皮肤干, 皮肤过敏. The skin of a fruit is 皮. Care words use 肤: 护肤 (skin care), 肤色 (skin color).
column6: Dōngtiān wǒ de pífū hěn gān.
column7: My skin is very dry in winter.
column9: A person's skin: 皮膚白, 皮膚乾, 皮膚過敏. The skin of a fruit is 皮. Care words use 膚: 護膚 (skin care), 膚色 (skin color).

column3: Toenails are 脚指甲. You 剪 or 涂 them; 指甲油 is nail polish. 甲 also names the first of a list, so 甲方 is Party A in a contract. 甲 began as a picture of an animal's hard shell or scales, or a suit of armor.
column4: 他的指甲太长了，该剪了。
column5: 他的指甲太長了，該剪了。
column6: Tā de zhǐjia tài cháng le, gāi jiǎn le.
column7: His nails are too long and need cutting.
column9: Toenails are 腳指甲. You 剪 or 塗 them; 指甲油 is nail polish. 甲 also names the first of a list, so 甲方 is Party A in a contract. 甲 began as a picture of an animal's hard shell or scales, or a suit of armor.

column3: The sound and pace of walking: 脚步声, 加快脚步, 放慢脚步. Figuratively the pace of change: 跟上时代的脚步. 步 recurs in 散步, 跑步 and 进步.
column6: Tā jiākuài le jiǎobù.
column7: He quickened his pace.
column9: The sound and pace of walking: 腳步聲, 加快腳步, 放慢腳步. Figuratively the pace of change: 跟上時代的腳步. 步 recurs in 散步, 跑步 and 進步.

column3: Any facial hair: 留胡子, 刮胡子, 大胡子 (a full beard), 小胡子 (a mustache). 胡须 is the formal word.
column6: Bàba měitiān zǎoshang guā húzi.
column7: Dad shaves every morning.
column9: Any facial hair: 留鬍子, 刮鬍子, 大鬍子 (a full beard), 小鬍子 (a mustache). 鬍鬚 is the formal word.

column3: Giving or receiving with both hands is polite: 双手递给他, 双手接过. 双 as "both" starts many body words: 双脚, 双眼, 双臂. It also counts pairs: 一双鞋, 一双筷子.
column6: Tā yòng shuāngshǒu jiēguò lǐwù.
column7: He took the gift with both hands.
column9: Giving or receiving with both hands is polite: 雙手遞給他, 雙手接過. 雙 as "both" starts many body words: 雙腳, 雙眼, 雙臂. It also counts pairs: 一雙鞋, 一雙筷子.

column3: Common with 出, 流 and 擦: 出汗, 擦汗, 满头大汗; 汗水 is the more vivid word. A cold sweat is 冷汗. On the internet, 汗 alone is a groan of speechless embarrassment.
column6: Tā cā le cā tóu shàng de hàn.
column7: He wiped the sweat from his head.
column9: Common with 出, 流 and 擦: 出汗, 擦汗, 滿頭大汗; 汗水 is the more vivid word. A cold sweat is 冷汗. On the internet, 汗 alone is a groan of speechless embarrassment.

column3: A verb plus object, so 了 goes between: 出了很多汗, 出了一身汗. 出 plus a body fluid or product gives similar words: 出血, 出油, 出水. 流汗 stresses it running down.
column6: Tiān tài rè, wǒ yīzhí chūhàn.
column7: It's so hot that I keep sweating.
column9: A verb plus object, so 了 goes between: 出了很多汗, 出了一身汗. 出 plus a body fluid or product gives similar words: 出血, 出油, 出水. 流汗 stresses it running down.

column3: A precise, written word, used by doctors and in instructions: 身体部位, 受伤的部位, 疼痛部位. For a general part or share, 部分 is the word.
column6: Nǐ nǎ ge bùwèi bù shūfu?
column7: Which part of your body feels unwell?
column9: A precise, written word, used by doctors and in instructions: 身體部位, 受傷的部位, 疼痛部位. For a general part or share, 部分 is the word.

column3: Nerve in medicine (神经痛, 神经系统) and, colloquially, unhinged: 神经病 and 你神经啊 are insulting. 神经紧张 means on edge. Avoid the insults with people you do not know.
column6: Tā yǒudiǎn shénjīng jǐnzhāng.
column7: He is a bit nervous.
column9: Nerve in medicine (神經痛, 神經系統) and, colloquially, unhinged: 神經病 and 你神經啊 are insulting. 神經緊張 means on edge. Avoid the insults with people you do not know.

column3: Written. The gaze and, figuratively, outlook: 目光短浅 (shortsighted), 吸引目光. In speech 眼光 is also used, more for judgment: 有眼光. 目 is the eye in written words: 目睹, 注目.
column4: 大家的目光都落在她身上。
column5: 大家的目光都落在她身上。
column6: Dàjiā de mùguāng dōu luò zài tā shēnshang.
column7: Everyone's eyes were on her.
column9: Written. The gaze and, figuratively, outlook: 目光短淺 (shortsighted), 吸引目光. In speech 眼光 is also used, more for judgment: 有眼光. 目 is the eye in written words: 目睹, 注目.

column3: A virus, biological or computer: 新冠病毒, 电脑病毒, with 感染 and 传播. Antivirus is 杀毒. 毒 alone is poison: 消毒, 中毒, 毒品. Bacteria are a different word, 细菌.
column6: Zhè zhǒng bìngdú chuánbō de hěn kuài.
column7: This virus spreads quickly.
column9: A virus, biological or computer: 新冠病毒, 電腦病毒, with 感染 and 傳播. Antivirus is 殺毒. 毒 alone is poison: 消毒, 中毒, 毒品. Bacteria are a different word, 細菌.

column3: Both verb and noun: 做按摩, 按摩一下肩膀 (一下 softens it), 足底按摩. 按 recurs in 按钮, 按键 and 按时 (on time).
column6: Wǒ xiǎng qù ànmó yīxià jiānbǎng.
column7: I'd like to get my shoulders massaged.
column9: Both verb and noun: 做按摩, 按摩一下肩膀 (一下 softens it), 足底按摩. 按 recurs in 按鈕, 按鍵 and 按時 (on time).

column3: Usually met in 咳嗽, a cough: 咳嗽药, 咳嗽得很厉害. Alone it is the act, with a count: 咳了几声.
column4: 他咳了几声，然后继续讲。
column5: 他咳了幾聲，然後繼續講。
column6: Tā ké le jǐ shēng, ránhòu jìxù jiǎng.
column7: He coughed a few times, then went on talking.
column9: Usually met in 咳嗽, a cough: 咳嗽藥, 咳嗽得很厲害. Alone it is the act, with a count: 咳了幾聲.

column3: Outpatients; you 挂号 first, then 看门诊. Opposite 住院, staying in. 诊 recurs in 急诊 (emergency), 诊所 (clinic) and 就诊 (formal, to seek treatment).
column4: 她今天上午去医院看门诊。
column5: 她今天上午去醫院看門診。
column6: Tā jīntiān shàngwǔ qù yīyuàn kàn ménzhěn.
column7: This morning she went to the hospital to see a doctor at the outpatient clinic.
column9: Outpatients; you 掛號 first, then 看門診. Opposite 住院, staying in. 診 recurs in 急診 (emergency), 診所 (clinic) and 就診 (formal, to seek treatment).

column3: Doctors diagnose, but so do tests and machines. The illness follows with 为 or 出: 诊断为肺炎, 诊断出问题. Related: 误诊 for a wrong diagnosis, 确诊 for a confirmed one.
column6: Yīshēng zhěnduàn tā dé le fèiyán.
column7: The doctor diagnosed him with pneumonia.
column9: Doctors diagnose, but so do tests and machines. The illness follows with 為 or 出: 診斷為肺炎, 診斷出問題. Related: 誤診 for a wrong diagnosis, 確診 for a confirmed one.

column3: The counterpart of 西药. You 吃 or 煎 it, buy it at a 中药店, and a 中医 is the doctor who prescribes it. Most 中药 is plants, but also includes minerals and animal parts.
column6: Zhè wǎn zhōngyào hěn kǔ.
column7: This bowl of herbal medicine is very bitter.
column9: The counterpart of 西藥. You 吃 or 煎 it, buy it at a 中藥店, and a 中醫 is the doctor who prescribes it. Most 中藥 is plants, but also includes minerals and animal parts.

column3: A written, medical word for an injection, found on labels and in reports. In everyday talk people say 打针, and a syringe is 注射器. 射 began as a bow and an arrow, to shoot a bow.
column6: Hùshi gěi tā zhùshè le yìmiáo.
column7: The nurse gave him a vaccine injection.
column9: A written, medical word for an injection, found on labels and in reports. In everyday talk people say 打針, and a syringe is 注射器. 射 began as a bow and an arrow, to shoot a bow.

column3: It takes no object: 他中毒了. The cause goes before it: 食物中毒, 煤气中毒. 中暑 (heatstroke) works the same way. Here 中 means to be struck by something unwelcome, and with this meaning it is read zhòng.
column4: 吃了不新鲜的鱼，他中毒了。
column5: 吃了不新鮮的魚，他中毒了。
column6: Chī le bù xīnxiān de yú, tā zhòngdú le.
column7: He ate stale fish and got food poisoning.
column9: It takes no object: 他中毒了. The cause goes before it: 食物中毒, 煤氣中毒. 中暑 (heatstroke) works the same way. Here 中 means to be struck by something unwelcome, and with this meaning it is read zhòng.

column3: Use it as a predicate (这种草有毒) or before a noun with 的 (有毒的蘑菇). Warnings say 有毒，请勿食用, and the opposite is 无毒. Same 有 + noun pattern as 有害 and 有用.
column6: Zhè zhǒng mógu yǒudú, bié chī.
column7: This mushroom is poisonous, don't eat it.
column9: Use it as a predicate (這種草有毒) or before a noun with 的 (有毒的蘑菇). Warnings say 有毒，請勿食用, and the opposite is 無毒. Same 有 + noun pattern as 有害 and 有用.

column3: Takes 对 for who or what is harmed: 吸烟对身体有害. Formal, common in warnings and news; the opposite is 有益. Also 有害物质 for harmful substances.
column6: Xīyān duì shēntǐ yǒuhài.
column7: Smoking is harmful to health.
column9: Takes 對 for who or what is harmed: 吸煙對身體有害. Formal, common in warnings and news; the opposite is 有益. Also 有害物質 for harmful substances.

column3: Beyond poison (毒蛇 a venomous snake), it means illegal drugs: 毒品, 吸毒. It is also the 毒 of 病毒, a virus. Vicious: 毒辣, 嘴毒 for a sharp tongue.
column6: Zhè zhǒng shé de dú hěn qiáng.
column7: The venom of this snake is very strong.
column9: Beyond poison (毒蛇 a venomous snake), it means illegal drugs: 毒品, 吸毒. It is also the 毒 of 病毒, a virus. Vicious: 毒辣, 嘴毒 for a sharp tongue.

column3: A computer word first: 杀毒软件 is antivirus software, and 杀毒 is also the scan-and-clean command. For disinfecting a cup or a wound the word is 消毒.
column4: 我的电脑装了杀毒软件。
column5: 我的電腦裝了殺毒軟體。
column6: Wǒ de diànnǎo zhuāng le shādú ruǎnjiàn.
column7: I installed antivirus software on my computer.
column9: A computer word first: 殺毒軟件 is antivirus software, and 殺毒 is also the scan-and-clean command. For disinfecting a cup or a wound the word is 消毒.

column3: The thing cleaned comes before it with 给 or 把: 给手消毒, 把杯子消毒, not 消毒手. 了 can go between: 消了毒. 消 means to get rid of, as in 消炎, to reduce inflammation. 消毒水 is disinfectant.
column4: 用之前要先把杯子消毒。
column5: 用之前要先把杯子消毒。
column6: Yòng zhīqián yào xiān bǎ bēizi xiāodú.
column7: Disinfect the cup before use.
column9: The thing cleaned comes before it with 給 or 把: 給手消毒, 把杯子消毒, not 消毒手. 了 can go between: 消了毒. 消 means to get rid of, as in 消炎, to reduce inflammation. 消毒水 is disinfectant.

column3: The pattern is 对 + trigger + 过敏: 对花粉过敏. It is also a noun in 过敏反应 and 皮肤过敏, and a figure of speech for oversensitive: 他对批评很过敏.
column6: Wǒ duì huāfěn guòmǐn.
column7: I am allergic to pollen.
column9: The pattern is 對 + trigger + 過敏: 對花粉過敏. It is also a noun in 過敏反應 and 皮膚過敏, and a figure of speech for oversensitive: 他對批評很過敏.

column3: Care that keeps things in shape: 保养汽车 servicing a car, 保养皮肤 skin care. It is upkeep, not repair; for fixing something broken you say 维修.
column6: Qìchē yào dìngqī bǎoyǎng.
column7: A car needs regular servicing.
column9: Care that keeps things in shape: 保養汽車 servicing a car, 保養皮膚 skin care. It is upkeep, not repair; for fixing something broken you say 維修.

column3: The noun for sleep in health and science: you 睡觉 in speech but talk about good or poor 睡眠, with 质量, 不足, 改善. On a phone or computer 睡眠 is also sleep mode.
column6: Tā zuìjìn shuìmián bù hǎo.
column7: He hasn't been sleeping well lately.
column9: The noun for sleep in health and science: you 睡覺 in speech but talk about good or poor 睡眠, with 質量, 不足, 改善. On a phone or computer 睡眠 is also sleep mode.

column3: Praise or a wish: 祝你健康长寿. It works as an adjective (他很长寿), and 长寿面 are the noodles eaten on a birthday. 寿 alone is life or birthday, as in 寿命 and 祝寿.
column4: 爷爷活到九十岁，真长寿。
column5: 爺爺活到九十歲，真長壽。
column6: Yéye huó dào jiǔshí suì, zhēn chángshòu.
column7: Grandpa lived to ninety, a long life indeed.
column9: Praise or a wish: 祝你健康長壽. It works as an adjective (他很長壽), and 長壽麵 are the noodles eaten on a birthday. 壽 alone is life or birthday, as in 壽命 and 祝壽.

column3: Stamina over time: 体力好, 体力差, 恢复体力. 体力活 and 体力劳动 are manual work. 力气 is the muscle for one task, such as lifting something heavy.
column6: Pá shān xūyào hěn hǎo de tǐlì.
column7: Climbing mountains takes good stamina.
column9: Stamina over time: 體力好, 體力差, 恢復體力. 體力活 and 體力勞動 are manual work. 力氣 is the muscle for one task, such as lifting something heavy.

column3: To let something out of the mouth: 吐痰 spit phlegm, 吐骨头 spit out bones, 吐舌头 stick out the tongue. Figuratively, to say or speak out: 吐露, and 吐字清楚 for clear speech. Vomiting is a separate entry of the same character.
column6: Qǐng bùyào suídì tǔ tán.
column7: Please do not spit on the ground.
column9: To let something out of the mouth: 吐痰 spit phlegm, 吐骨頭 spit out bones, 吐舌頭 stick out the tongue. Figuratively, to say or speak out: 吐露, and 吐字清楚 for clear speech. Vomiting is a separate entry of the same character.

column3: 想吐 is to feel like throwing up, 吐了 is that it happened, and 呕吐 is the written word. 上吐下泻 is the medical set phrase for vomiting and diarrhea. Spitting is a separate entry of the same character.
column6: Tā zuò chē shí juéde xiǎng tù.
column7: He felt like throwing up in the car.
column9: 想吐 is to feel like throwing up, 吐了 is that it happened, and 嘔吐 is the written word. 上吐下瀉 is the medical set phrase for vomiting and diarrhea. Spitting is a separate entry of the same character.

column3: Followed by the habit: 戒烟, 戒酒, 戒糖. It also means to be on guard, as in 戒备 and 警戒, and it is the 戒 of 戒指, a ring. It shows a halberd and two hands, to hold up a weapon as warning.
column6: Tā zhōngyú bǎ yān jiè le.
column7: He finally gave up smoking.
column9: Followed by the habit: 戒煙, 戒酒, 戒糖. It also means to be on guard, as in 戒備 and 警戒, and it is the 戒 of 戒指, a ring. It shows a halberd and two hands, to hold up a weapon as warning.

column3: Warm and slightly literary, used when speaking of parents and children: 儿女双全, 为儿女操心. In daily speech 孩子 is more usual, and 子女 is the plainer formal term.
column4: 他的儿女都在国外工作。
column5: 他的兒女都在國外工作。
column6: Tā de érnǚ dōu zài guówài gōngzuò.
column7: His children all work abroad.
column9: Warm and slightly literary, used when speaking of parents and children: 兒女雙全, 為兒女操心. In daily speech 孩子 is more usual, and 子女 is the plainer formal term.

column3: Counts generations: 大一辈, 差一辈, and 长辈, 晚辈, 前辈, 平辈. 辈分 is your rank by generation. For a lifetime 辈 rarely stands alone; the word is 一辈子.
column6: Tā bǐ wǒ dà yī bèi.
column7: He is one generation older than me.
column9: Counts generations: 大一輩, 差一輩, and 長輩, 晚輩, 前輩, 平輩. 輩分 is your rank by generation. For a lifetime 輩 rarely stands alone; the word is 一輩子.

column3: Spoken. It goes before the verb (一辈子也忘不了) or after it as a duration (活了一辈子, 干了一辈子). Related: 这辈子 in this life and 下辈子 in the next.
column4: 我一辈子都不会忘记你。
column5: 我一輩子都不會忘記你。
column6: Wǒ yībèizi dōu bù huì wàngjì nǐ.
column7: I will never forget you as long as I live.
column9: Spoken. It goes before the verb (一輩子也忘不了) or after it as a duration (活了一輩子, 幹了一輩子). Related: 這輩子 in this life and 下輩子 in the next.

column3: The neutral noun for age: 年龄大, 年龄限制, 年龄段. To ask someone, do not say 年龄: ask 你多大？ or politely to an older person 您多大年纪？
column6: Zhège yóuxì yǒu niánlíng xiànzhì.
column7: This game has an age limit.
column9: The neutral noun for age: 年齡大, 年齡限制, 年齡段. To ask someone, do not say 年齡: ask 你多大？ or politely to an older person 您多大年紀？

column3: The person concerned, in person: 本人到场, 必须本人去. After a pronoun it stresses: 我本人, 他本人. On forms and in notices it can mean I, the writer: 本人签名.
column6: Bàn zhè jiàn shì bìxū běnrén qù.
column7: You must go in person to handle this.
column9: The person concerned, in person: 本人到場, 必須本人去. After a pronoun it stresses: 我本人, 他本人. On forms and in notices it can mean I, the writer: 本人簽名.

column3: A chatty, friendly word for a group you belong to or address: 大伙儿听我说. 大家 is the neutral equivalent. 大伙儿 is the northern erhua form of 大伙, which is also common, especially in writing.
column6: Dàhuǒr yīqǐ lái bāngmáng ba.
column7: Let's all help together.
column9: A chatty, friendly word for a group you belong to or address: 大伙兒聽我說. 大家 is the neutral equivalent. 大伙兒 is the northern erhua form of 大伙, which is also common, especially in writing.

column3: The neutral or formal word, used before nouns: 男性员工, 男性用品. For a plain man it is 男人. 性 here is sex or gender, as in 性别 and 女性.
column4: 这家公司的男性员工比较多。
column5: 這家公司的男性員工比較多。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de nánxìng yuángōng bǐjiào duō.
column7: This company has more male employees.
column9: The neutral or formal word, used before nouns: 男性員工, 男性用品. For a plain man it is 男人. 性 here is sex or gender, as in 性別 and 女性.

column3: The polite, general word where 女人 may sound blunt: 现代女性, 女性朋友, 女性用品. 女士 is a title (Ms., lady), and 妇女 sounds official, as in 妇女节.
column4: 现代女性的工作压力很大。
column5: 現代女性的工作壓力很大。
column6: Xiàndài nǚxìng de gōngzuò yālì hěn dà.
column7: Modern women are under a lot of pressure at work.
column9: The polite, general word where 女人 may sound blunt: 現代女性, 女性朋友, 女性用品. 女士 is a title (Ms., lady), and 婦女 sounds official, as in 婦女節.

column3: Used in news and formal writing, always with a modifier: 专业人士, 知名人士, 各界人士. It is not the word for a person in speech; say 人 or 那个人. 士 began as a picture of a war axe, and later came to mean officer and intellectual.
column4: 参加会议的有各界人士。
column5: 參加會議的有各界人士。
column6: Cānjiā huìyì de yǒu gèjiè rénshì.
column7: People from all walks of life attended the meeting.
column9: Used in news and formal writing, always with a modifier: 專業人士, 知名人士, 各界人士. It is not the word for a person in speech; say 人 or 那個人. 士 began as a picture of a war axe, and later came to mean officer and intellectual.

column3: A person who matters (重要人物, 大人物, 小人物 a nobody) and also a character in a novel or film: 小说里的人物. 历史人物 are figures of history.
column4: 他是这个领域的重要人物。
column5: 他是這個領域的重要人物。
column6: Tā shì zhège lǐngyù de zhòngyào rénwù.
column7: He is an important figure in this field.
column9: A person who matters (重要人物, 大人物, 小人物 a nobody) and also a character in a novel or film: 小說裡的人物. 歷史人物 are figures of history.

column3: Stresses belonging to the nation, in economic and political phrases: 国民经济, 国民收入, 国民素质. 公民 is the legal citizen with rights and duties.
column4: 国民的生活水平提高了。
column5: 國民的生活水平提高了。
column6: Guómín de shēnghuó shuǐpíng tígāo le.
column7: The living standard of the people has risen.
column9: Stresses belonging to the nation, in economic and political phrases: 國民經濟, 國民收入, 國民素質. 公民 is the legal citizen with rights and duties.

column3: Official and political language: 人民群众 are ordinary people as opposed to leaders. In everyday speech use 大家 or 人们 instead. 群 is written with 羊 and means a herd of sheep or a group.
column6: Tā hěn liǎojiě qúnzhòng de xūyào.
column7: He understands well what the people need.
column9: Official and political language: 人民群眾 are ordinary people as opposed to leaders. In everyday speech use 大家 or 人們 instead. 群 is written with 羊 and means a herd of sheep or a group.

column3: Either a noun (他是个天才) or a modifier (天才儿童, 音乐天才). 人才 is different: a capable person an employer wants, as in 招聘人才.
column4: 这个孩子是个音乐天才。
column5: 這個孩子是個音樂天才。
column6: Zhège háizi shì ge yīnyuè tiāncái.
column7: This child is a musical genius.
column9: Either a noun (他是個天才) or a modifier (天才兒童, 音樂天才). 人才 is different: a capable person an employer wants, as in 招聘人才.

column3: Idol, someone admired, mostly a singer, actor or athlete: 我的偶像, 偶像剧 "idol drama", 偶像歌手, 追星 "follow a star". It can also mean an idol statue to be worshiped, in its first sense. 偶 is "image, a figure" and 像 "likeness".
column6: Tā de ǒuxiàng shì yī wèi gēshǒu.
column7: Her idol is a singer.
column9: Idol, someone admired, mostly a singer, actor or athlete: 我的偶像, 偶像劇 "idol drama", 偶像歌手, 追星 "follow a star". It can also mean an idol statue to be worshiped, in its first sense. 偶 is "image, a figure" and 像 "likeness".

column3: Anyone who lives nearby, not only next door; 隔壁 is the home or person right next door. 邻 also appears in 邻国 neighboring country and 邻近 nearby.
column6: Wǒ de línjū shì yī wèi lǎoshī.
column7: My neighbor is a teacher.
column9: Anyone who lives nearby, not only next door; 隔壁 is the home or person right next door. 鄰 also appears in 鄰國 neighboring country and 鄰近 nearby.

column3: A formal modifier before a noun: 终身学习, 终身职位. 终身大事 is the big event of a lifetime, meaning marriage. 一辈子 is the spoken equivalent and goes before verbs.
column4: 我们要养成终身学习的习惯。
column5: 我們要養成終身學習的習慣。
column6: Wǒmen yào yǎngchéng zhōngshēn xuéxí de xíguàn.
column7: We should develop the habit of lifelong learning.
column9: A formal modifier before a noun: 終身學習, 終身職位. 終身大事 is the big event of a lifetime, meaning marriage. 一輩子 is the spoken equivalent and goes before verbs.

column3: The everyday word for the animal, counted with 头. 象 alone is bound, as in 象牙 ivory and 象鼻 trunk. 象 began as a picture of an elephant.
column6: Dàxiàng de bízi hěn cháng.
column7: The elephant's trunk is very long.
column9: The everyday word for the animal, counted with 頭. 象 alone is bound, as in 象牙 ivory and 象鼻 trunk. 象 began as a picture of an elephant.

column3: The full name is more formal or scientific; people say 熊猫 for short. 小熊猫 is the red panda. Counted with 只. The panda is China's 国宝, found mostly in Sichuan.
column6: Dàxióngmāo xǐhuan chī zhúzi.
column7: Giant pandas like to eat bamboo.
column9: The full name is more formal or scientific; people say 熊貓 for short. 小熊貓 is the red panda. Counted with 隻. The panda is China's 國寶, found mostly in Sichuan.

column3: 熊 alone is the everyday word for a bear (一只熊), and it is in 北极熊 and 熊猫. Northern slang: 你真熊 means you are a coward, and 熊孩子 is a bratty kid.
column6: Dōngtiān, xióng huì zài dòng lǐ shuìjiào.
column7: In winter bears sleep in caves.
column9: 熊 alone is the everyday word for a bear (一隻熊), and it is in 北極熊 and 熊貓. Northern slang: 你真熊 means you are a coward, and 熊孩子 is a bratty kid.

column3: Alone in the zodiac (属猴, 猴年) and in compounds; the animal in speech is 猴子. Calling a lively child 小猴子 is affectionate.
column6: Tā shǔ hóu, wǒ shǔ hǔ.
column7: He was born in the year of the monkey, I in the year of the tiger.
column9: Alone in the zodiac (屬猴, 猴年) and in compounds; the animal in speech is 猴子. Calling a lively child 小猴子 is affectionate.

column3: The animal is 老虎; 虎 alone is in the zodiac (属虎, 虎年) and in set phrases like 虎头蛇尾, a strong start and weak finish, and 马马虎虎, so-so.
column6: Wǒ shǔ hǔ, nǐ shǔ shénme?
column7: I was born in the year of the tiger. What about you?
column9: The animal is 老虎; 虎 alone is in the zodiac (屬虎, 虎年) and in set phrases like 虎頭蛇尾, a strong start and weak finish, and 馬馬虎虎, so-so.

column3: The animal in speech is 老鼠; 鼠 alone is in the zodiac (属鼠) and compounds. A computer mouse is 鼠标 on the mainland and 滑鼠 in Taiwan. The top of 鼠 is a rat's open mouth with its teeth showing, and below it are the feet and the tail.
column6: Tā shǔ shǔ, wǒ shǔ niú.
column7: He was born in the year of the rat, I in the year of the ox.
column9: The animal in speech is 老鼠; 鼠 alone is in the zodiac (屬鼠) and compounds. A computer mouse is 鼠標 on the mainland and 滑鼠 in Taiwan. The top of 鼠 is a rat's open mouth with its teeth showing, and below it are the feet and the tail.

column3: In a sentence the animal is 兔子 (一只兔子); 兔 alone is in the zodiac (属兔, 兔年) and in words like 野兔 hare and 小白兔.
column6: Tā shǔ tù, wǒ shǔ lóng.
column7: He was born in the year of the rabbit, I in the year of the dragon.
column9: In a sentence the animal is 兔子 (一隻兔子); 兔 alone is in the zodiac (屬兔, 兔年) and in words like 野兔 hare and 小白兔.

column3: Counted with 条: 一条蛇. 蛇年 is the year of the snake, and 画蛇添足 is the idiom for spoiling something by adding what is not needed. The right part 它 was also the original picture of a snake.
column6: Cǎocóng lǐ yǒu yī tiáo shé.
column7: There is a snake in the grass.
column9: Counted with 條: 一條蛇. 蛇年 is the year of the snake, and 畫蛇添足 is the idiom for spoiling something by adding what is not needed. The right part 它 was also the original picture of a snake.

column3: Counted with 只. 鸭 alone is bound, as in 烤鸭 and 鸭蛋. 赶鸭子上架 is the idiom for forcing someone into a job they cannot do.
column6: Chítáng lǐ yǒu jǐ zhī yāzi.
column7: There are some ducks in the pond.
column9: Counted with 隻. 鴨 alone is bound, as in 烤鴨 and 鴨蛋. 趕鴨子上架 is the idiom for forcing someone into a job they cannot do.

column3: In speech the plant is 竹子. 竹 alone is for the material and compounds, such as 竹筐 (bamboo basket) and 竹林 (bamboo grove). 竹 is a picture of two bamboo stalks with leaves.
column6: Xióngmāo měitiān chī hěn duō zhúzi.
column7: Pandas eat a lot of bamboo every day.
column9: In speech the plant is 竹子. 竹 alone is for the material and compounds, such as 竹筐 (bamboo basket) and 竹林 (bamboo grove). 竹 is a picture of two bamboo stalks with leaves.

column3: 桃花运 is luck in romance, while 烂桃花 are troublesome flirtations.
column4: 春天，公园里的桃花开了。
column5: 春天，公園裡的桃花開了。
column6: Chūntiān, gōngyuán lǐ de táohuā kāi le.
column7: In spring the peach blossoms in the park are out.
column9: 桃花運 is luck in romance, while 爛桃花 are troublesome flirtations.

column3: Fruit + 树 names the tree (苹果树, 梨树), and fruit + 花 the blossom (桃花). Trees are counted with 棵.
column6: Yuànzi lǐ zhòng zhe yī kē táoshù.
column7: A peach tree is planted in the yard.
column9: Fruit + 樹 names the tree (蘋果樹, 梨樹), and fruit + 花 the blossom (桃花). Trees are counted with 棵.

column3: Here 化 is the verb to turn into: turned to stone. 化石燃料 is fossil fuel, and 活化石 a living fossil, for an old species or custom still around.
column4: 博物馆里有一块恐龙化石。
column5: 博物館裡有一塊恐龍化石。
column6: Bówùguǎn lǐ yǒu yī kuài kǒnglóng huàshí.
column7: There is a dinosaur fossil in the museum.
column9: Here 化 is the verb to turn into: turned to stone. 化石燃料 is fossil fuel, and 活化石 a living fossil, for an old species or custom still around.

column3: Biological evolution (进化论), also used for technology and systems. The result takes 成: 进化成…. Opposite 退化. Taiwan prefers 演化 for biological evolution.
column6: Shēngwù bùduàn de jìnhuà.
column7: Living things keep evolving.
column9: Biological evolution (進化論), also used for technology and systems. The result takes 成: 進化成…. Opposite 退化. Taiwan prefers 演化 for biological evolution.

column3: Mostly in compounds and with verbs of landing: 靠岸, 上岸. 对岸 is the opposite bank, and 两岸 the two banks, a common phrase for the two sides of the Taiwan Strait.
column6: Chuán kào àn le.
column7: The boat has reached the shore.
column9: Mostly in compounds and with verbs of landing: 靠岸, 上岸. 對岸 is the opposite bank, and 兩岸 the two banks, a common phrase for the two sides of the Taiwan Strait.

column3: Contrasts with 水里 and 船上. 岸边 is at the water's edge; 岸上 is up on the land. Same pattern: place + 上 for on or over it, as in 桌上 and 河上.
column6: Rénmen zhàn zài ànshang kàn chuán.
column7: People stand on the bank and watch the boats.
column9: Contrasts with 水裡 and 船上. 岸邊 is at the water's edge; 岸上 is up on the land. Same pattern: place + 上 for on or over it, as in 桌上 and 河上.

column3: A vast grassland. A lawn or small grassy patch is 草地. The 原 is the plain in 平原 (flatland) and 高原 (plateau).
column6: Cǎoyuán shàng yǒu hěn duō niú hé yáng.
column7: There are many cows and sheep on the grassland.
column9: A vast grassland. A lawn or small grassy patch is 草地. The 原 is the plain in 平原 (flatland) and 高原 (plateau).

column3: Sand desert, as in 撒哈拉沙漠; 沙漠化 is desertification. 沙 alone is sand (沙子, 沙滩) and also lends its sound to 沙发, sofa. 漠 mostly appears in 沙漠 and 冷漠.
column6: Shāmò lǐ hěn nán zhǎodào shuǐ.
column7: It is hard to find water in the desert.
column9: Sand desert, as in 撒哈拉沙漠; 沙漠化 is desertification. 沙 alone is sand (沙子, 沙灘) and also lends its sound to 沙發, sofa. 漠 mostly appears in 沙漠 and 冷漠.

column3: A plateau, as in 青藏高原; 高原反应 is altitude sickness. It pairs with 平原, the plain: the same 原, high versus flat, and 草原 is grassland.
column4: 西藏位于世界上最高的高原。
column5: 西藏位於世界上最高的高原。
column6: Xīzàng wèiyú shìjiè shàng zuì gāo de gāoyuán.
column7: Tibet lies on the highest plateau in the world.
column9: A plateau, as in 青藏高原; 高原反應 is altitude sickness. It pairs with 平原, the plain: the same 原, high versus flat, and 草原 is grassland.

column3: A wide flat stretch of land, as in 华北平原. Compare 高原 plateau and 草原 grassland: the same 原, with 平 flat in front. The opposite landscape is 山区.
column6: Zhèlǐ shì yī piàn dà píngyuán.
column7: This is a big plain.
column9: A wide flat stretch of land, as in 華北平原. Compare 高原 plateau and 草原 grassland: the same 原, with 平 flat in front. The opposite landscape is 山區.

column3: Often in news about poverty, roads or tourism: 偏远山区, 山区的孩子. The same 区 ends 郊区 and 地区. 山 is a picture of three mountain peaks.
column6: Shānqū de dōngtiān hěn lěng.
column7: Winters in the mountains are cold.
column9: Often in news about poverty, roads or tourism: 偏遠山區, 山區的孩子. The same 區 ends 郊區 and 地區. 山 is a picture of three mountain peaks.

column3: Bound and nearly always in compounds: 泉水 spring water, 温泉 hot spring, 山泉. Alone it needs a measure word, as in 一眼泉. It is built from 白, a spring mouth, and 水, water: water flowing from the source of a spring.
column6: Shānjiǎo xià yǒu yī yǎn quán.
column7: There is a spring at the foot of the mountain.
column9: Bound and nearly always in compounds: 泉水 spring water, 溫泉 hot spring, 山泉. Alone it needs a measure word, as in 一眼泉. It is built from 白, a spring mouth, and 水, water: water flowing from the source of a spring.

column3: A ditch or gully: 水沟 a drain, 山沟 a mountain gully. It also turns figurative: 沟通 is to communicate, a channel between people, and 代沟 is a generation gap.
column6: Lùbiān yǒu yī tiáo xiǎo gōu.
column7: There is a small ditch by the road.
column9: A ditch or gully: 水溝 a drain, 山溝 a mountain gully. It also turns figurative: 溝通 is to communicate, a channel between people, and 代溝 is a generation gap.

column3: Nearly always has a modifier in front: 危险地带, 沿海地带, 缓冲地带 buffer zone; and 灰色地带 is a gray area in the figurative sense. 带 began as a picture of a woven belt, and it also means an area or zone.
column4: 这是一个危险地带，请小心。
column5: 這是一個危險地帶，請小心。
column6: Zhè shì yī gè wēixiǎn dìdài, qǐng xiǎoxīn.
column7: This is a danger zone, please be careful.
column9: Nearly always has a modifier in front: 危險地帶, 沿海地帶, 緩衝地帶 buffer zone; and 灰色地帶 is a gray area in the figurative sense. 帶 began as a picture of a woven belt, and it also means an area or zone.

column3: The lay of the land, whether mountains, plains or hills: 地形复杂, 地形图 topographic map, 熟悉地形. The same 形 is in 形状 shape and 情形 situation.
column6: Zhèlǐ de dìxíng hěn fùzá.
column7: The terrain here is very complex.
column9: The lay of the land, whether mountains, plains or hills: 地形複雜, 地形圖 topographic map, 熟悉地形. The same 形 is in 形狀 shape and 情形 situation.

column3: A lake held back by a dam, for water supply, irrigation or power: 修水库, 水库大坝. 库 is the storing part of 仓库 warehouse, 车库 garage and 数据库 database.
column6: Zhège shuǐkù wèi quán chéng gōngshuǐ.
column7: This reservoir supplies water to the whole city.
column9: A lake held back by a dam, for water supply, irrigation or power: 修水庫, 水庫大壩. 庫 is the storing part of 倉庫 warehouse, 車庫 garage and 數據庫 database.

column3: The Pole or the Arctic region: 北极熊 polar bear, 北极圈 Arctic Circle. 极 is also "extremely": 极了 after an adjective (好极了), or 极 before one (极大).
column6: Běijí de dōngtiān fēicháng lěng.
column7: Winters in the Arctic are extremely cold.
column9: The Pole or the Arctic region: 北極熊 polar bear, 北極圈 Arctic Circle. 極 is also "extremely": 極了 after an adjective (好極了), or 極 before one (極大).

column3: Antarctica as well as the South Pole: 南极洲 is the continent, and 去南极考察 is an expedition there.
column6: Qǐ'é shēnghuó zài nánjí.
column7: Penguins live in the Antarctic.
column9: Antarctica as well as the South Pole: 南極洲 is the continent, and 去南極考察 is an expedition there.

column3: The border area, or the border in general: 边境线, 边境贸易, 守卫边境, common in news on customs and security. The boundary line itself is 边界. 境 is territory, as in 国境 and 环境 environment.
column4: 两国的边境已经关闭了。
column5: 兩國的邊境已經關閉了。
column6: Liǎng guó de biānjìng yǐjīng guānbì le.
column7: The border between the two countries has been closed.
column9: The border area, or the border in general: 邊境線, 邊境貿易, 守衛邊境, common in news on customs and security. The boundary line itself is 邊界. 境 is territory, as in 國境 and 環境 environment.

column3: A somewhat formal word for a defined part of a space, a country or a field: 不同区域, 区域经济 regional economy, 禁止区域. In plain talk, 地方 is the everyday word for a place.
column6: Zhège qūyù jìnzhǐ tíngchē.
column7: Parking is forbidden in this area.
column9: A somewhat formal word for a defined part of a space, a country or a field: 不同區域, 區域經濟 regional economy, 禁止區域. In plain talk, 地方 is the everyday word for a place.

column3: Both banks of a river, and "both sides of the Strait", Taiwan and the mainland: 河的两岸, 海峡两岸. In news 两岸关系 "cross-strait relations" is the usual phrase. 两 is "two", a pair as in 两边, and 岸 "shore".
column6: Hé de liǎng'àn dōu shì lǜshù.
column7: Both banks of the river are lined with green trees.
column9: Both banks of a river, and "both sides of the Strait", Taiwan and the mainland: 河的兩岸, 海峽兩岸. In news 兩岸關係 "cross-strait relations" is the usual phrase. 兩 is "two", a pair as in 兩邊, and 岸 "shore".

column3: Chinese says south-north, the reverse of English: 南北方向, 南北差异, 走南闯北 to travel everywhere. It can also mean the whole length: 南北长. 北 began as two men back to back, with the sense "back"; "north" is derived from "back".
column6: Zhè tiáo lù shì nánběi fāngxiàng de.
column7: This road runs north to south.
column9: Chinese says south-north, the reverse of English: 南北方向, 南北差異, 走南闖北 to travel everywhere. It can also mean the whole length: 南北長. 北 began as two men back to back, with the sense "back"; "north" is derived from "back".

column3: A hole or a cave: 山洞, 洞口 the mouth of a cave, 老鼠洞, 黑洞 black hole. It is counted with 个. When numbers are read out, 洞 is a spoken 0, as 幺 is for 1.
column6: Wàzi shàng yǒu yī gè dòng.
column7: There is a hole in the sock.
column9: A hole or a cave: 山洞, 洞口 the mouth of a cave, 老鼠洞, 黑洞 black hole. It is counted with 個. When numbers are read out, 洞 is a spoken 0, as 么 is for 1.

column3: Rain as a supply, in farming and weather talk: 雨水充足, 雨水少, 收集雨水 to collect rainwater. The verb "to rain" is 下雨. It is also the name of a solar term in February. 雨 began as a cloud with drops of rain falling from it.
column6: Jīnnián de yǔshuǐ hěn chōngzú.
column7: There has been plenty of rain this year.
column9: Rain as a supply, in farming and weather talk: 雨水充足, 雨水少, 收集雨水 to collect rainwater. The verb "to rain" is 下雨. It is also the name of a solar term in February. 雨 began as a cloud with drops of rain falling from it.

column3: Weather conditions and the science of them: 气象台 weather station, 气象预报 forecast. Figuratively it is the look or atmosphere of a scene: 新气象 a new look. Everyday weather is 天气.
column4: 气象部门预报明天有大雨。
column5: 氣象部門預報明天有大雨。
column6: Qìxiàng bùmén yùbào míngtiān yǒu dàyǔ.
column7: The weather bureau forecasts heavy rain for tomorrow.
column9: Weather conditions and the science of them: 氣象台 weather station, 氣象預報 forecast. Figuratively it is the look or atmosphere of a scene: 新氣象 a new look. Everyday weather is 天氣.

column3: Sunny and cloudless, for sky and weather only: 天气晴朗, 晴朗的天空. A cheerful person is 开朗, not 晴朗. 晴 has the sun 日 in it, and 朗 has the moon 月.
column4: 今天天气晴朗，适合爬山。
column5: 今天天氣晴朗，適合爬山。
column6: Jīntiān tiānqì qínglǎng, shìhé pá shān.
column7: The weather is clear today, good for climbing a mountain.
column9: Sunny and cloudless, for sky and weather only: 天氣晴朗, 晴朗的天空. A cheerful person is 開朗, not 晴朗. 晴 has the sun 日 in it, and 朗 has the moon 月.

column3: Alone it turns up in short phrases and compounds: 天气暖了, 暖手 to warm your hands, 暖气 central heating. The spoken adjective is 暖和, and 暖 is gentler than 热. The sun 日 on its left is the part that carries the meaning.
column6: Chūntiān lái le, tiānqì nuǎn le.
column7: Spring has come and the weather is warm.
column9: Alone it turns up in short phrases and compounds: 天氣暖了, 暖手 to warm your hands, 暖氣 central heating. The spoken adjective is 暖和, and 暖 is gentler than 熱. The sun 日 on its left is the part that carries the meaning.

column3: The word for heat in weather reports: 高温预警 heat warning, 高温天气. It also covers technical heat: 高温消毒. The opposite is 低温. 温 is temperature in 体温 and 气温 too. 温 represents a person bathing in a container full of warm water.
column6: Xiàtiān cháng yǒu gāowēn tiānqì.
column7: In summer there are often very hot days.
column9: The word for heat in weather reports: 高溫預警 heat warning, 高溫天氣. It also covers technical heat: 高溫消毒. The opposite is 低溫. 溫 is temperature in 體溫 and 氣溫 too. 溫 represents a person bathing in a container full of warm water.

column3: In the air or sky: 在空中飞, 空中交通 air traffic; 空中楼阁 is a castle in the air, an unrealistic plan.
column6: Yī zhī niǎo zài kōngzhōng fēi.
column7: A bird is flying in the air.
column9: In the air or sky: 在空中飛, 空中交通 air traffic; 空中樓閣 is a castle in the air, an unrealistic plan.

column3: The Moon as a body in science and news: 登上月球, 月球表面. In daily talk and poems the moon you see is 月亮. 球 is a ball or globe, as in 地球 and 足球. 月 began as a picture of a crescent moon.
column4: 他梦想有一天能去月球。
column5: 他夢想有一天能去月球。
column6: Tā mèngxiǎng yǒu yī tiān néng qù yuèqiú.
column7: He dreams of going to the moon one day.
column9: The Moon as a body in science and news: 登上月球, 月球表面. In daily talk and poems the moon you see is 月亮. 球 is a ball or globe, as in 地球 and 足球. 月 began as a picture of a crescent moon.

column3: Outer space: 太空旅行 "space travel", 进入太空 "enter space", 太空站 "space station". 太 "very big" (a 大 with a dot) + 空 "sky". Taiwan uses 太空人 for astronaut; the mainland says 宇航员 or 航天员. Slightly more everyday than 宇宙, which is "the universe".
column4: 宇航员在太空工作了半年。
column5: 宇航員在太空工作了半年。
column6: Yǔhángyuán zài tàikōng gōngzuò le bàn nián.
column7: The astronaut worked in space for half a year.
column9: Outer space: 太空旅行 "space travel", 進入太空 "enter space", 太空站 "space station". 太 "very big" (a 大 with a dot) + 空 "sky". Taiwan uses 太空人 for astronaut; the mainland says 宇航員 or 航天員. Slightly more everyday than 宇宙, which is "the universe".

column3: Artificial or natural: 人造卫星, 卫星电视, 卫星定位 satellite positioning, and a planet's moon. 卫 is "to guard", also in 卫生间 restroom.
column6: Zhè kē wèixīng rào zhe dìqiú zhuàn.
column7: This satellite goes around the Earth.
column9: Artificial or natural: 人造衛星, 衛星電視, 衛星定位 satellite positioning, and a planet's moon. 衛 is "to guard", also in 衛生間 restroom.

column3: Astronomy as a field of study: 天文学, 天文台 observatory, 天文望远镜. 天文数字 is an astronomical figure, a huge number. 文 began as a man with a painted or tattooed chest, a pattern or marking.
column6: Tā duì tiānwén hěn gǎn xìngqù.
column7: He is very interested in astronomy.
column9: Astronomy as a field of study: 天文學, 天文台 observatory, 天文望遠鏡. 天文數字 is an astronomical figure, a huge number. 文 began as a man with a painted or tattooed chest, a pattern or marking.

column3: Light as it falls in a place or on a photo: 光线好, 光线暗, 光线太强. 光 alone is light in general. 线 is thread or line, so this is a ray. 光 is fire 火 over a kneeling person, stressing the shining of light.
column6: Zhège fángjiān guāngxiàn hěn hǎo.
column7: This room has good light.
column9: Light as it falls in a place or on a photo: 光線好, 光線暗, 光線太強. 光 alone is light in general. 線 is thread or line, so this is a ray. 光 is fire 火 over a kneeling person, stressing the shining of light.

column3: Gray, and figuratively murky: 灰色地带 a gray area. Before a noun 的 is optional: 灰色外套 or 灰色的外套. 灰 is a hand 又 and fire 火: fire that can be touched with the hand, ash.
column4: 天空是灰色的，好像要下雨。
column5: 天空是灰色的，好像要下雨。
column6: Tiānkōng shì huīsè de, hǎoxiàng yào xià yǔ.
column7: The sky is gray and it looks like rain.
column9: Gray, and figuratively murky: 灰色地帶 a gray area. Before a noun 的 is optional: 灰色外套 or 灰色的外套. 灰 is a hand 又 and fire 火: fire that can be touched with the hand, ash.

column3: Can stand before a noun on its own: 紫裙子, 紫葡萄. The noun is 紫色. Also in 紫外线 ultraviolet and the Forbidden City, 紫禁城.
column6: Tā mǎi le yī tiáo zǐ qúnzi.
column7: She bought a purple skirt.
column9: Can stand before a noun on its own: 紫裙子, 紫葡萄. The noun is 紫色. Also in 紫外線 ultraviolet and the Forbidden City, 紫禁城.

column3: An old color word covering green, blue and black by the thing: 青草, 青天 blue sky, 青菜, 青丝 black hair. It also means young: 青年, 青春. Mostly in compounds. One explanation reads it as 生, growing plants, plus 丹, cinnabar: the color of growing plants.
column6: Chūntiān, shān shàng de cǎo qīng le.
column7: In spring the grass on the mountain turns green.
column9: An old color word covering green, blue and black by the thing: 青草, 青天 blue sky, 青菜, 青絲 black hair. It also means young: 青年, 青春. Mostly in compounds. One explanation reads it as 生, growing plants, plus 丹, cinnabar: the color of growing plants.

column3: Bright, for light, rooms, eyes and colors: 明亮的眼睛, 灯光明亮. 亮 alone is "to light up" or "to get light": 天亮了, 亮灯. 明 puts the sun 日 and the moon 月 together: the sun just rising and the moon not yet set, dawn.
column6: Jiàoshì lǐ hěn míngliàng.
column7: The classroom is bright.
column9: Bright, for light, rooms, eyes and colors: 明亮的眼睛, 燈光明亮. 亮 alone is "to light up" or "to get light": 天亮了, 亮燈. 明 puts the sun 日 and the moon 月 together: the sun just rising and the moon not yet set, dawn.

column3: For colors that catch the eye, often of flowers, clothes and fruit: 色彩鲜艳, 鲜艳的花. 鲜 alone also means fresh, as in 新鲜.
column4: 公园里开满了鲜艳的花。
column5: 公園裡開滿了鮮艷的花。
column6: Gōngyuán lǐ kāi mǎn le xiānyàn de huā.
column7: The park is full of brightly colored flowers.
column9: For colors that catch the eye, often of flowers, clothes and fruit: 色彩鮮艷, 鮮艷的花. 鮮 alone also means fresh, as in 新鮮.

column3: Community, neighborhood: 社区服务 "community service", 社区医院, 我们社区. It usually means the residential area managed by a neighborhood committee, a unit of city life in China. 社 is the "earth spirit" (the old altar of the land) and 区 "area". 小区 is a mainland word for a housing complex.
column4: 我们社区有一个小图书馆。
column5: 我們社區有一個小圖書館。
column6: Wǒmen shèqū yǒu yī gè xiǎo túshūguǎn.
column7: Our neighborhood has a small library.
column9: Community, neighborhood: 社區服務 "community service", 社區醫院, 我們社區. It usually means the residential area managed by a neighborhood committee, a unit of city life in China. 社 is the "earth spirit" (the old altar of the land) and 區 "area". 小區 is a mainland word for a housing complex.

column3: A wharf or pier for boats: 货运码头 freight dock, 港口码头. It can mean a trade hub too. Elsewhere 码 is a number or code: 号码, 密码 password. The 头 is a noun suffix, with no tone here, as in 石头.
column6: Chuán tíng zài mǎtou biān.
column7: The boat is moored at the dock.
column9: A wharf or pier for boats: 貨運碼頭 freight dock, 港口碼頭. It can mean a trade hub too. Elsewhere 碼 is a number or code: 號碼, 密碼 password. The 頭 is a noun suffix, with no tone here, as in 石頭.

column3: On the mainland an ordinary mid-range hotel, often state-run; 酒店 is usually more upscale and 旅馆 a small inn. In Taiwan 宾馆 usually means a cheap short-stay or love hotel; an ordinary hotel is 饭店 or 酒店. 馆 names a kind of establishment: 饭馆 restaurant, 图书馆 library, 大使馆 embassy.
column4: 我们住在车站附近的宾馆。
column5: 我們住在車站附近的賓館。
column6: Wǒmen zhù zài chēzhàn fùjìn de bīnguǎn.
column7: We are staying at a hotel near the station.
column9: On the mainland an ordinary mid-range hotel, often state-run; 酒店 is usually more upscale and 旅館 a small inn. In Taiwan 賓館 usually means a cheap short-stay or love hotel; an ordinary hotel is 飯店 or 酒店. 館 names a kind of establishment: 飯館 restaurant, 圖書館 library, 大使館 embassy.

column3: Counted with 座 or 家: 一座博物馆, 参观博物馆. The Palace Museum is 故宫博物院, which uses 院. 博 is "wide", also in 博士 and 博览会.
