column9: To enjoy an experience fully and slowly: 享受生活, 享受美食, 享受假期. 我很享受 on its own is a common spoken way to say you are loving it. It also has a formal side, to have a right to something: 享受待遇, 享受優惠.

column3: To enjoy something as beauty (欣赏音乐, 欣赏风景) or to think highly of a person's quality (欣赏他的勇气). It carries taste or respect; for simply liking food or a hobby, say 喜欢.
column6: Wǒ hěn xīnshǎng tā de yǒngqì.
column7: I admire his courage.
column9: To enjoy something as beauty (欣賞音樂, 欣賞風景) or to think highly of a person's quality (欣賞他的勇氣). It carries taste or respect; for simply liking food or a hobby, say 喜歡.

column3: Energy as a quality of life: 充满活力, 有活力, 缺乏活力. Positive, and said of people, teams, cities, companies and even a design. For physical energy to get things done, 精力 is the word, as in 精力充沛.
column6: Niánqīngrén chōngmǎn huólì.
column7: Young people are full of energy.
column9: Energy as a quality of life: 充滿活力, 有活力, 缺乏活力. Positive, and said of people, teams, cities, companies and even a design. For physical energy to get things done, 精力 is the word, as in 精力充沛.

column3: The bond between people or countries, a little formal: 深厚的友谊, 珍惜友谊, 建立友谊. It names the relationship; for being friends, say 朋友: 我们是朋友. It also gives 友谊赛, a friendly match. One old reading takes 友 as two hands, hence friendship.
column4: 我们的友谊已经十年了。
column5: 我們的友誼已經十年了。
column6: Wǒmen de yǒuyì yǐjīng shí nián le.
column7: Our friendship has lasted ten years.
column9: The bond between people or countries, a little formal: 深厚的友誼, 珍惜友誼, 建立友誼. It names the relationship; for being friends, say 朋友: 我們是朋友. It also gives 友誼賽, a friendly match. One old reading takes 友 as two hands, hence friendship.

column3: Leisure, mostly as a modifier: 休闲活动, 休闲时间, 休闲服 (casual clothes), 休闲餐厅. In speech 休息 is to rest; 休闲 is spending free time pleasantly, with a walk, tea or a hobby, as the opposite of work. 休 began as a man leaning against a tree, resting.
column4: 周末我喜欢去公园散散步，休闲一下。
column5: 週末我喜歡去公園散散步，休閒一下。
column6: Zhōumò wǒ xǐhuan qù gōngyuán sànsan bù, xiūxián yīxià.
column7: On weekends I like to take a walk in the park and relax a bit.
column9: Leisure, mostly as a modifier: 休閒活動, 休閒時間, 休閒服 (casual clothes), 休閒餐廳. In speech 休息 is to rest; 休閒 is spending free time pleasantly, with a walk, tea or a hobby, as the opposite of work. 休 began as a man leaning against a tree, resting.

column3: Wit and funniness: 很幽默, 幽默感, 幽默的人. Lighter and cleverer than 搞笑, which is silly, goofy comedy.
column6: Tā shuōhuà hěn yōumò.
column7: He is very funny when he talks.
column9: Wit and funniness: 很幽默, 幽默感, 幽默的人. Lighter and cleverer than 搞笑, which is silly, goofy comedy.

column3: A warm, informal word, a bit old-fashioned, for a carefree life or mood: 过得很快活, 快活的日子. It is not for greetings or holidays; for "Happy New Year" the word is 快乐.
column6: Tāmen guò de hěn kuàihuo.
column7: They lead a happy life.
column9: A warm, informal word, a bit old-fashioned, for a carefree life or mood: 過得很快活, 快活的日子. It is not for greetings or holidays; for "Happy New Year" the word is 快樂.

column3: Lively and outgoing, praise for children and young people: 活泼可爱, 性格活泼. Also for styles, colors and layouts that feel cheerful, and in chemistry it means reactive. The opposite for a person is 文静 (quiet and gentle).
column6: Zhège háizi hěn huópo.
column7: This child is very lively.
column9: Lively and outgoing, praise for children and young people: 活潑可愛, 性格活潑. Also for styles, colors and layouts that feel cheerful, and in chemistry it means reactive. The opposite for a person is 文靜 (quiet and gentle).

column3: Free of things to do right now: 他今天很闲, 闲着 (sit idle). Different from 有空, which is time available for plans. 闲聊 is idle chat and 闲人 an idler, with a faint put-down; 闲话 is gossip.
column6: Tā jīntiān hěn xián.
column7: He has nothing to do today.
column9: Free of things to do right now: 他今天很閒, 閒著 (sit idle). Different from 有空, which is time available for plans. 閒聊 is idle chat and 閒人 an idler, with a faint put-down; 閒話 is gossip.

column3: A spoken word for a short break in the middle of work or a walk: 歇一会儿, 歇歇, 歇口气 (catch your breath), 歇脚 (stop to rest). 歇业 means a shop closes for business. For a long rest, 休息 is the word.
column6: Lèi le jiù xiē yīhuìr ba.
column7: If you're tired, rest a while.
column9: A spoken word for a short break in the middle of work or a walk: 歇一會兒, 歇歇, 歇口氣 (catch your breath), 歇腳 (stop to rest). 歇業 means a shop closes for business. For a long rest, 休息 is the word.

column3: Quick to learn and quick-witted: 聪明的孩子, 很聪明. Said of animals too, and of ideas: 聪明的办法 is a smart way. 小聪明 is petty cleverness, a mild put-down. An early form of 聪 was a heart 心 with a big dot on top for a hole, said to show an open heart and an open mind.
column6: Zhège háizi hěn cōngming.
column7: This child is very clever.
column9: Quick to learn and quick-witted: 聰明的孩子, 很聰明. Said of animals too, and of ideas: 聰明的辦法 is a smart way. 小聰明 is petty cleverness, a mild put-down. An early form of 聰 was a heart 心 with a big dot on top for a hole, said to show an open heart and an open mind.

column3: Silly or foolish, and often fond: 你真傻 is gentle teasing, 傻孩子 is what a parent says. Unlike 笨 (slow, dull), 傻 is about daft behavior: 傻笑, 装傻 (play dumb). 傻眼 is to be stunned speechless.
column6: Wǒ zhēn shǎ, zěnme méi xiǎngdào ne?
column7: How silly of me not to have thought of it!
column9: Silly or foolish, and often fond: 你真傻 is gentle teasing, 傻孩子 is what a parent says. Unlike 笨 (slow, dull), 傻 is about daft behavior: 傻笑, 裝傻 (play dumb). 傻眼 is to be stunned speechless.

column3: Bold, in praise: 大胆尝试 (dare to try), 大胆的想法, 大胆地说. Said sharply, 大胆！ means "how dare you!" Chinese puts courage in the gallbladder, so 胆子大 says the same thing about a person.
column4: 她大胆地说出了自己的想法。
column5: 她大膽地說出了自己的想法。
column6: Tā dàdǎn de shuōchū le zìjǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
column7: She boldly spoke her mind.
column9: Bold, in praise: 大膽嘗試 (dare to try), 大膽的想法, 大膽地說. Said sharply, 大膽！ means "how dare you!" Chinese puts courage in the gallbladder, so 膽子大 says the same thing about a person.

column3: Chinese puts courage in the gallbladder, so 胆子小 says the same thing of a person. 胆小鬼 is a coward, said teasingly to a child or friend. The opposites are 大胆 and 胆子大.
column6: Tā dǎnxiǎo, bù gǎn yī ge rén shuì.
column7: He is timid and dares not sleep alone.
column9: Chinese puts courage in the gallbladder, so 膽子小 says the same thing of a person. 膽小鬼 is a coward, said teasingly to a child or friend. The opposites are 大膽 and 膽子大.

column3: Polite in a way that keeps some distance. 别客气 or 不用客气 answers thanks and tells a guest to relax; 太客气了 thanks someone for a gift; 跟我客气什么 means "no need to stand on ceremony with me." Among close friends, being 客气 can feel cold.
column6: Bùyòng kèqi, qǐng zuò.
column7: No need to stand on ceremony; please sit.
column9: Polite in a way that keeps some distance. 別客氣 or 不用客氣 answers thanks and tells a guest to relax; 太客氣了 thanks someone for a gift; 跟我客氣什麼 means "no need to stand on ceremony with me." Among close friends, being 客氣 can feel cold.

column3: Both a noun (manners) and an adjective (polite): 有礼貌, 没礼貌, 讲礼貌. The person comes after 对: 对客人很有礼貌. Adults tell children 要有礼貌. 礼貌用语 are the polite phrases like 请 and 谢谢. 礼 shows performing rites at an altar.
column6: Duì lǎorén yào yǒu lǐmào.
column7: You must be polite to old people.
column9: Both a noun (manners) and an adjective (polite): 有禮貌, 沒禮貌, 講禮貌. The person comes after 對: 對客人很有禮貌. Adults tell children 要有禮貌. 禮貌用語 are the polite phrases like 請 and 謝謝. 禮 shows performing rites at an altar.

column3: Steady diligence in study or work: 勤奋学习. 勤劳 is hardworking, mostly physical labor (勤劳的农民), and 努力 is the everyday word for trying hard at anything.
column6: Tā xuéxí hěn qínfèn.
column7: He studies diligently.
column9: Steady diligence in study or work: 勤奮學習. 勤勞 is hardworking, mostly physical labor (勤勞的農民), and 努力 is the everyday word for trying hard at anything.

column3: Praise for staying open to advice and criticism: 虚心学习, 虚心接受批评 (accept criticism with an open mind), 他很虚心. The opposite is 骄傲 or 自满.
column6: Tā xūxīn de tīngqǔ yìjiàn.
column7: He listens humbly to advice.
column9: Praise for staying open to advice and criticism: 虛心學習, 虛心接受批評 (accept criticism with an open mind), 他很虛心. The opposite is 驕傲 or 自滿.

column3: Sincere in a warm, open way, stronger than 诚实 (honest, truthful): 真诚的道歉, 真诚地感谢, 待人真诚. Before a verb it takes 地, before a noun 的.
column6: Tā de dàoqiàn hěn zhēnchéng.
column7: His apology was sincere.
column9: Sincere in a warm, open way, stronger than 誠實 (honest, truthful): 真誠的道歉, 真誠地感謝, 待人真誠. Before a verb it takes 地, before a noun 的.

column3: Mild and gentle, not weak: a person's nature (性格温和), a tone of voice, a climate (气候温和), even a medicine or soap. The opposite for a person is 暴躁, hot-tempered. 温 is said to show a person bathing in a container full of warm water.
column6: Tā shuōhuà de shēngyīn hěn wēnhé.
column7: He has a gentle voice.
column9: Mild and gentle, not weak: a person's nature (性格溫和), a tone of voice, a climate (氣候溫和), even a medicine or soap. The opposite for a person is 暴躁, hot-tempered. 溫 is said to show a person bathing in a container full of warm water.

column3: A spoken word that swings between praise and warning. 你真厉害 is "you're amazing"; a 厉害的老师 is a tough, formidable teacher. After 得 it means severely: 疼得厉害, 冷得厉害.
column6: Tā de Yīngyǔ shuō de zhēn lìhai.
column7: His English is really impressive.
column9: A spoken word that swings between praise and warning. 你真厲害 is "you're amazing"; a 厲害的老師 is a tough, formidable teacher. After 得 it means severely: 疼得厲害, 冷得厲害.

column3: Stern about behavior, said of a person or a punishment: 严厉的老师, 严厉批评, 严厉打击 (crack down hard). Harsher than 严格, which only means strict about rules and standards; a 严格 teacher can still be kind.
column6: Lǎoshī duì xuésheng hěn yánlì.
column7: The teacher is very strict with his students.
column9: Stern about behavior, said of a person or a punishment: 嚴厲的老師, 嚴厲批評, 嚴厲打擊 (crack down hard). Harsher than 嚴格, which only means strict about rules and standards; a 嚴格 teacher can still be kind.

column3: Serious in manner, topic or mood: 表情严肃, 严肃的话题, 严肃地说. Of a rule, 严肃处理 means to handle it strictly. It is about gravity; 认真 is about taking care in doing something (认真学习).
column6: Tā de biǎoqíng hěn yánsù.
column7: His expression is very serious.
column9: Serious in manner, topic or mood: 表情嚴肅, 嚴肅的話題, 嚴肅地說. Of a rule, 嚴肅處理 means to handle it strictly. It is about gravity; 認真 is about taking care in doing something (認真學習).

column3: Firm in will or belief, never a hard object (that is 坚硬): 态度坚定, 坚定的信念, 坚定地说. As a verb it means to strengthen one's resolve: 坚定信心. 坚定不移 is "unwavering."
column6: Tā de tàidù hěn jiāndìng.
column7: Her attitude is very firm.
column9: Firm in will or belief, never a hard object (that is 堅硬): 態度堅定, 堅定的信念, 堅定地說. As a verb it means to strengthen one's resolve: 堅定信心. 堅定不移 is "unwavering."

column3: A serious, written word for hard conditions of living or work: 艰苦的环境, 生活艰苦, 艰苦奋斗 (work hard through difficulty). It suits a poor or remote place, not a hard exam or puzzle; for a hard problem, 困难 is the word.
column6: Shānqū de shēnghuó hěn jiānkǔ.
column7: Life in the mountains is hard.
column9: A serious, written word for hard conditions of living or work: 艱苦的環境, 生活艱苦, 艱苦奮鬥 (work hard through difficulty). It suits a poor or remote place, not a hard exam or puzzle; for a hard problem, 困難 is the word.

column3: A person's temper or disposition: 脾气好 and 脾气不好 describe character. 发脾气 is to lose one's temper, and 他有脾气 means he has a temper. 好脾气 is a good-natured person.
column6: Tā píqi bù hǎo, róngyì shēngqì.
column7: He has a bad temper and gets angry easily.
column9: A person's temper or disposition: 脾氣好 and 脾氣不好 describe character. 發脾氣 is to lose one's temper, and 他有脾氣 means he has a temper. 好脾氣 is a good-natured person.

column3: Social standing and dignity in others' eyes: 爱面子 (care about appearances), 给面子 (show respect by agreeing), 丢面子 or 没面子 (lose face). 看在我的面子上 means "do it for my sake." 面 began as a man's face with an eye exaggerated.
column6: Tā hěn ài miànzi.
column7: He cares a lot about saving face.
column9: Social standing and dignity in others' eyes: 愛面子 (care about appearances), 給面子 (show respect by agreeing), 丟面子 or 沒面子 (lose face). 看在我的面子上 means "do it for my sake." 面 began as a man's face with an eye exaggerated.

column3: Its biggest use is thanks for effort: 你辛苦了 to someone who worked or traveled for you, 您辛苦了 more politely, 辛苦你了 when asking a favor. For a gift or a small kindness, use 谢谢 instead.
column4: 你辛苦了，快坐下休息吧。
column5: 你辛苦了，快坐下休息吧。
column6: Nǐ xīnkǔ le, kuài zuòxià xiūxi ba.
column7: You've worked hard; sit down and rest.
column9: Its biggest use is thanks for effort: 你辛苦了 to someone who worked or traveled for you, 您辛苦了 more politely, 辛苦你了 when asking a favor. For a gift or a small kindness, use 謝謝 instead.

column3: Patience as a noun after 有 or 没有 (很有耐心), and as an adverb with 地 (耐心地解释). The opposite is 不耐烦 (impatient). The 耐 is the one in 耐用 (durable) and 耐看 (good-looking over time).
column6: Lǎoshī hěn yǒu nàixīn.
column7: The teacher is very patient.
column9: Patience as a noun after 有 or 沒有 (很有耐心), and as an adverb with 地 (耐心地解釋). The opposite is 不耐煩 (impatient). The 耐 is the one in 耐用 (durable) and 耐看 (good-looking over time).

column3: Sensitive to senses (对声音敏感) or to a topic: 敏感话题 is a touchy subject. Of a person, 太敏感 means taking things too personally; in business or science it is praise: 对数字很敏感 (good with numbers).
column6: Tā duì shēngyīn hěn mǐngǎn.
column7: She is very sensitive to sound.
column9: Sensitive to senses (對聲音敏感) or to a topic: 敏感話題 is a touchy subject. Of a person, 太敏感 means taking things too personally; in business or science it is praise: 對數字很敏感 (good with numbers).

column3: Formal, and only before a noun: 不良习惯, 不良影响, 不良少年 (a delinquent), 营养不良 (malnutrition). In plain speech you say 这个习惯不好, not 很不良.
column6: Áoyè shì yī zhǒng bùliáng xíguàn.
column7: Staying up late is a bad habit.
column9: Formal, and only before a noun: 不良習慣, 不良影響, 不良少年 (a delinquent), 營養不良 (malnutrition). In plain speech you say 這個習慣不好, not 很不良.

column3: Cultivation of character that shows in behavior: 有修养 (well-bred), 个人修养, 文化修养. A person with it stays calm and polite in a quarrel. It can also mean trained skill in a field: 艺术修养. For manners taught by parents, 教养 is closer.
column4: 他是一个很有修养的人。
column5: 他是一個很有修養的人。
column6: Tā shì yī ge hěn yǒu xiūyǎng de rén.
column7: He is a very cultivated person.
column9: Cultivation of character that shows in behavior: 有修養 (well-bred), 個人修養, 文化修養. A person with it stays calm and polite in a quarrel. It can also mean trained skill in a field: 藝術修養. For manners taught by parents, 教養 is closer.

column3: Spoken: something costs real effort or is beyond you. It sits after 得 or 觉得: 做得吃力, 学得很吃力. 吃 here is not eating but bearing, as in 吃苦. 吃力不讨好 is working hard and getting no thanks.
column4: 这个工作他做得有点吃力。
column5: 這個工作他做得有點吃力。
column6: Zhège gōngzuò tā zuò de yǒudiǎn chīlì.
column7: He finds this job a bit of a strain.
column9: Spoken: something costs real effort or is beyond you. It sits after 得 or 覺得: 做得吃力, 學得很吃力. 吃 here is not eating but bearing, as in 吃苦. 吃力不討好 is working hard and getting no thanks.

column3: A polite, written word for calling on someone to show respect: 拜访老师, 拜访客户, 登门拜访 (visit at their home). For dropping in on a friend, 去看 or 去找 is the everyday phrase.
column4: 我明天去拜访一位老师。
column5: 我明天去拜訪一位老師。
column6: Wǒ míngtiān qù bàifǎng yī wèi lǎoshī.
column7: Tomorrow I am going to call on a teacher.
column9: A polite, written word for calling on someone to show respect: 拜訪老師, 拜訪客戶, 登門拜訪 (visit at their home). For dropping in on a friend, 去看 or 去找 is the everyday phrase.

column3: The pattern is 邀请 + person + 参加 + event: 邀请我参加婚礼. It is also a noun: 接受邀请, 邀请函 (invitation letter). More formal than 请, and used for events and trips; for a meal you pay for, say 请你吃饭.
column4: 他邀请我参加他的婚礼。
column5: 他邀請我參加他的婚禮。
column6: Tā yāoqǐng wǒ cānjiā tā de hūnlǐ.
column7: He invited me to his wedding.
column9: The pattern is 邀請 + person + 參加 + event: 邀請我參加婚禮. It is also a noun: 接受邀請, 邀請函 (invitation letter). More formal than 請, and used for events and trips; for a meal you pay for, say 請你吃飯.

column3: The person comes right after 陪, then what you do together: 陪妈妈去医院, 陪孩子玩, 陪朋友聊天. It is giving your company and time. 陪同 is the formal version for guests, 陪伴 for steady companionship.
column6: Wǒ péi māma qù yīyuàn.
column7: I am going to the hospital with my mother.
column9: The person comes right after 陪, then what you do together: 陪媽媽去醫院, 陪孩子玩, 陪朋友聊天. It is giving your company and time. 陪同 is the formal version for guests, 陪伴 for steady companionship.

column3: Rare alone except in 送礼 and 收礼 (gifts). At the end of a word it names a ceremony, as in 婚礼 and 葬礼; at the start it can mean manners (礼貌, 礼节). A present is a 礼物.
column4: 他送了我一份礼，我也回了一份礼。
column5: 他送了我一份禮，我也回了一份禮。
column6: Tā sòng le wǒ yī fèn lǐ, wǒ yě huí le yī fèn lǐ.
column7: He gave me a gift, and I gave one back.
column9: Rare alone except in 送禮 and 收禮 (gifts). At the end of a word it names a ceremony, as in 婚禮 and 葬禮; at the start it can mean manners (禮貌, 禮節). A present is a 禮物.

column3: Formal and written; in speech, say 送. It suits a gift from an organization or a respected person, and lives on in 赠品 (a freebie with a purchase) and 捐赠 (to donate).
column6: Lǎoshī zèng gěi wǒ yī běn shū.
column7: The teacher gave me a book as a present.
column9: Formal and written; in speech, say 送. It suits a gift from an organization or a respected person, and lives on in 贈品 (a freebie with a purchase) and 捐贈 (to donate).

column3: The shop-window word for freebies: 赠送礼品, 买一送一, 免费赠送. A friend handing over a present just says 送; 赠送 sounds like a promotion or an official gift.
column4: 买满一百元，商店赠送一个小礼物。
column5: 買滿一百元，商店贈送一個小禮物。
column6: Mǎi mǎn yībǎi yuán, shāngdiàn zèngsòng yī ge xiǎo lǐwù.
column7: Spend a hundred yuan and the store gives you a small gift.
column9: The shop-window word for freebies: 贈送禮品, 買一送一, 免費贈送. A friend handing over a present just says 送; 贈送 sounds like a promotion or an official gift.

column3: Offers something with respect or devotion: flowers to a teacher, blood to a hospital, a life to a cause. Both 向 + person + 献 + thing and 献给 + person are standard; for ordinary giving use 给 or 送. Common inside 贡献 and 奉献.
column4: 学生们向老师献了一束花。
column5: 學生們向老師獻了一束花。
column6: Xuéshengmen xiàng lǎoshī xiàn le yī shù huā.
column7: The students presented the teacher with a bunch of flowers.
column9: Offers something with respect or devotion: flowers to a teacher, blood to a hospital, a life to a cause. Both 向 + person + 獻 + thing and 獻給 + person are standard; for ordinary giving use 給 or 送. Common inside 貢獻 and 奉獻.

column3: Congratulates on something that has happened (a win, a wedding, a degree), with the person as object: 祝贺你. For good wishes ahead of time, 祝 alone does it: 祝你成功. The everyday spoken form is 恭喜.
column6: Zhùhè nǐ kǎoshàng le dàxué!
column7: Congratulations on getting into university!
column9: Congratulates on something that has happened (a win, a wedding, a degree), with the person as object: 祝賀你. For good wishes ahead of time, 祝 alone does it: 祝你成功. The everyday spoken form is 恭喜.

column3: Looks up to a person for age, character or position: 受人尊敬. 尊敬的 + title opens formal letters and speeches. For opinions, rules or rights, use 尊重, not 尊敬.
column6: Wǒmen dōu hěn zūnjìng tā.
column7: We all respect him.
column9: Looks up to a person for age, character or position: 受人尊敬. 尊敬的 + title opens formal letters and speeches. For opinions, rules or rights, use 尊重, not 尊敬.

column3: Treats a person, opinion, rule or right as worth consideration: 尊重隐私, 互相尊重. Unlike 尊敬, it needs no looking up to anyone; it only means not overriding or brushing aside.
column4: 我们要尊重别人的选择。
column5: 我們要尊重別人的選擇。
column6: Wǒmen yào zūnzhòng biéren de xuǎnzé.
column7: We must respect other people's choices.
column9: Treats a person, opinion, rule or right as worth consideration: 尊重隱私, 互相尊重. Unlike 尊敬, it needs no looking up to anyone; it only means not overriding or brushing aside.

column3: More formal and warmer than everyday 关心. Usually shown by an institution, leader or society toward people who need it: 关怀老人, 人文关怀. Between friends, 关心 is the natural word.
column6: Shèhuì yīnggāi duō guānhuái lǎorén.
column7: Society should show more care for the elderly.
column9: More formal and warmer than everyday 關心. Usually shown by an institution, leader or society toward people who need it: 關懷老人, 人文關懷. Between friends, 關心 is the natural word.

column3: Two uses: a noun for what comes back from effort or money (得到回报, 投资回报), and a verb for repaying kindness (回报社会). For warm personal gratitude, 报答 is the closer word.
column6: Tā de nǔlì dédào le huíbào.
column7: His efforts were rewarded.
column9: Two uses: a noun for what comes back from effort or money (得到回報, 投資回報), and a verb for repaying kindness (回報社會). For warm personal gratitude, 報答 is the closer word.

column3: Repays a good turn, with feeling: 报答父母, 无以报答. It is about gratitude to a person and sounds a little formal; 回报 is more about results and returns.
column4: 我一定会报答你的恩情。
column5: 我一定會報答你的恩情。
column6: Wǒ yīdìng huì bàodá nǐ de ēnqíng.
column7: I will repay your kindness for sure.
column9: Repays a good turn, with feeling: 報答父母, 無以報答. It is about gratitude to a person and sounds a little formal; 回報 is more about results and returns.

column3: A card sent for a holiday, birthday or wedding, now often as an e-card (电子贺卡). The same 卡 is in 银行卡 and 信用卡.
column4: 我给朋友寄了一张贺卡。
column5: 我給朋友寄了一張賀卡。
column6: Wǒ gěi péngyou jì le yī zhāng hèkǎ.
column7: I sent my friend a greeting card.
column9: A card sent for a holiday, birthday or wedding, now often as an e-card (電子賀卡). The same 卡 is in 銀行卡 and 信用卡.

column3: Shares something you enjoy or find useful: joy, experience, photos. It is also the 'share' button in apps. For splitting a cost or a burden, use 分担, not 分享.
column4: 我想和大家分享这个好消息。
column5: 我想和大家分享這個好消息。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng hé dàjiā fēnxiǎng zhège hǎo xiāoxi.
column7: I'd like to share this good news with everyone.
column9: Shares something you enjoy or find useful: joy, experience, photos. It is also the 'share' button in apps. For splitting a cost or a burden, use 分擔, not 分享.

column3: A written 'too', going before an adjective or verb: 过于紧张, 过于担心. It is for something undesirable or past what is right, so it is not said of praise. In speech, 太 does this job.
column4: 他过于紧张，说不出话来。
column5: 他過於緊張，說不出話來。
column6: Tā guòyú jǐnzhāng, shuō bu chū huà lái.
column7: He was too nervous to say a word.
column9: A written 'too', going before an adjective or verb: 過於緊張, 過於擔心. It is for something undesirable or past what is right, so it is not said of praise. In speech, 太 does this job.

column3: Goes before a verb or noun: 过度使用, 过度劳累, 过度饮酒. Neutral to negative. Do not mix it up with 过渡 (a transition), which has the same pinyin.
column4: 过度使用手机对眼睛不好。
column5: 過度使用手機對眼睛不好。
column6: Guòdù shǐyòng shǒujī duì yǎnjing bù hǎo.
column7: Overusing a phone is bad for the eyes.
column9: Goes before a verb or noun: 過度使用, 過度勞累, 過度飲酒. Neutral to negative. Do not mix it up with 過渡 (a transition), which has the same pinyin.

column3: Follows the quality it describes: 信心十足, 干劲十足. Before 的 it stresses completeness: 十足的傻瓜. The 十 means 'full' here, as it does in 十分 and 十全十美.
column6: Tā jīntiān xìnxīn shízú.
column7: He is full of confidence today.
column9: Follows the quality it describes: 信心十足, 幹勁十足. Before 的 it stresses completeness: 十足的傻瓜. The 十 means 'full' here, as it does in 十分 and 十全十美.

column3: Picks one item out of a group already mentioned: 尤其是苹果. It sits before an adjective, a verb or 是 + noun. 特别 just means very or particularly and needs no group to pick from.
column4: 我喜欢水果，尤其是苹果。
column5: 我喜歡水果，尤其是蘋果。
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan shuǐguǒ, yóuqí shì píngguǒ.
column7: I like fruit, especially apples.
column9: Picks one item out of a group already mentioned: 尤其是蘋果. It sits before an adjective, a verb or 是 + noun. 特別 just means very or particularly and needs no group to pick from.

column3: Written, and mostly before a verb in set requests: 稍等, 稍作休息. Also 稍大, 稍有不同. In speech the usual form is 稍微.
column4: 请稍等一下，我马上回来。
column5: 請稍等一下，我馬上回來。
column6: Qǐng shāo děng yīxià, wǒ mǎshàng huílái.
column7: Please wait a moment; I will be right back.
column9: Written, and mostly before a verb in set requests: 稍等, 稍作休息. Also 稍大, 稍有不同. In speech the usual form is 稍微.

column3: Goes before a verb or adjective, usually with 一点, 一下 or 有点 to soften it: 稍微休息一下, 稍微大一点. Handy in comparisons: 比昨天稍微冷一点. Less written than 稍.
column4: 今天比昨天稍微冷一点儿。
column5: 今天比昨天稍微冷一點兒。
column6: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān shāowēi lěng yīdiǎnr.
column7: Today is a little colder than yesterday.
column9: Goes before a verb or adjective, usually with 一點, 一下 or 有點 to soften it: 稍微休息一下, 稍微大一點. Handy in comparisons: 比昨天稍微冷一點. Less written than 稍.

column3: For something that nearly happened and did not. With an unwanted event the two forms agree: 差点儿摔倒 means 差点儿没摔倒. With a wanted one it is ambiguous even for natives (差点儿没考上), so say 差点儿就考上了 (nearly, but didn't) or 好不容易才考上 (barely did).
column6: Wǒ chàdiǎnr chídào le.
column7: I was almost late.
column9: For something that nearly happened and did not. With an unwanted event the two forms agree: 差點兒摔倒 means 差點兒沒摔倒. With a wanted one it is ambiguous even for natives (差點兒沒考上), so say 差點兒就考上了 (nearly, but didn't) or 好不容易才考上 (barely did).

column3: Means the same as 差点儿 but stresses how small the gap was. Often followed by 就 for a near miss: 差一点儿就赶上了, 'missed it by a hair'.
column4: 我差一点儿就赶上火车了。
column5: 我差一點兒就趕上火車了。
column6: Wǒ chàyīdiǎnr jiù gǎnshàng huǒchē le.
column7: I almost caught the train.
column9: Means the same as 差點兒 but stresses how small the gap was. Often followed by 就 for a near miss: 差一點兒就趕上了, 'missed it by a hair'.

column3: An adverb that gives the broad outline without detail: 大致相同, 大致了解, 大致上. A little formal. It can also modify a noun: 大致情况.
column6: Wǒ dàzhì kàn le yī biàn.
column7: I looked it over roughly.
column9: An adverb that gives the broad outline without detail: 大致相同, 大致了解, 大致上. A little formal. It can also modify a noun: 大致情況.

column3: States a minimum, in a spoken and flexible way: 起码要一年. Before a noun with 的 it means basic: 起码的礼貌, 起码的要求. 至少 is the neutral 'at least'; 起码 often hints that the bar is low.
column4: 起码要学一年才能说好。
column5: 起碼要學一年才能說好。
column6: Qǐmǎ yào xué yī nián cái néng shuō hǎo.
column7: It takes at least a year of study to speak well.
column9: States a minimum, in a spoken and flexible way: 起碼要一年. Before a noun with 的 it means basic: 起碼的禮貌, 起碼的要求. 至少 is the neutral 'at least'; 起碼 often hints that the bar is low.

column3: Two senses. Seldom, before a verb: 他难得来一次; or rare, 难得的机会. It also praises something not easy to find in a person: 这么年轻就这么稳重，真难得.
column6: Zhème hǎo de tiānqì hěn nándé.
column7: Such lovely weather is rare.
column9: Two senses. Seldom, before a verb: 他難得來一次; or rare, 難得的機會. It also praises something not easy to find in a person: 這麼年輕就這麼穩重，真難得.

column3: Written and formal, before a usually two-syllable verb: 难以置信, 难以接受, 难以入睡, 难以避免. It never takes 很; in speech, say 很难 + verb.
column6: Zhè zhǒng gǎnjué nányǐ xíngróng.
column7: This feeling is hard to describe.
column9: Written and formal, before a usually two-syllable verb: 難以置信, 難以接受, 難以入睡, 難以避免. It never takes 很; in speech, say 很難 + verb.

column3: Written, and often admiring effort: 来之不易, 实属不易. Before a verb it means not easily: 不易保存. 易 alone works as '-able' in words like 易懂 and 易碎.
column6: Zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ bùyì bǎocún.
column7: This fruit does not keep easily.
column9: Written, and often admiring effort: 來之不易, 實屬不易. Before a verb it means not easily: 不易保存. 易 alone works as '-able' in words like 易懂 and 易碎.

column3: Says a result follows naturally from the situation, mostly with a feeling: 不免紧张, 不免担心. Written. 难免 means nearly the same and is more common in speech.
column4: 第一次上台，他不免有些紧张。
column5: 第一次上臺，他不免有些緊張。
column6: Dìyī cì shàngtái, tā bùmiǎn yǒuxiē jǐnzhāng.
column7: On stage for the first time, he could not help being a little nervous.
column9: Says a result follows naturally from the situation, mostly with a feeling: 不免緊張, 不免擔心. Written. 難免 means nearly the same and is more common in speech.

column3: Goes before an adjective or verb: 尽可能早, 尽可能多, 尽可能地帮助. 尽量 means the same and is more common in speech.
column6: Qǐng jìnkěnéng zǎodiǎn lái.
column7: Please come as early as you can.
column9: Goes before an adjective or verb: 盡可能早, 盡可能多, 盡可能地幫助. 盡量 means the same and is more common in speech.

column3: Reading aloud clearly and with expression, a school exercise: 朗读课文, 朗读比赛. 读 alone can be silent; 朗诵 is reciting a poem or prose with feeling.
column4: 老师让我们大声朗读课文。
column5: 老師讓我們大聲朗讀課文。
column6: Lǎoshī ràng wǒmen dàshēng lǎngdú kèwén.
column7: The teacher had us read the text aloud.
column9: Reading aloud clearly and with expression, a school exercise: 朗讀課文, 朗讀比賽. 讀 alone can be silent; 朗誦 is reciting a poem or prose with feeling.

column3: Mostly inside compounds (回答, 答案, 答题). Alone it is fine in speech in result phrases: 答对, 答错, 答不上来. For a plain verb 'to reply', 回答 is usual.
column4: 老师问了一个问题，没人答得上来。
column5: 老師問了一個問題，沒人答得上來。
column6: Lǎoshī wèn le yī ge wèntí, méi rén dá de shànglái.
column7: The teacher asked a question and nobody could answer it.
column9: Mostly inside compounds (回答, 答案, 答題). Alone it is fine in speech in result phrases: 答對, 答錯, 答不上來. For a plain verb 'to reply', 回答 is usual.

column3: A formal reply, usually from an organization or person in charge to a question, request or proposal: 等待答复, 书面答复. It often means a definite yes or no. 回答 answers any ordinary question.
column6: Qǐng jǐnkuài dáfù wǒ.
column7: Please reply to me as soon as you can.
column9: A formal reply, usually from an organization or person in charge to a question, request or proposal: 等待答復, 書面答復. It often means a definite yes or no. 回答 answers any ordinary question.

column3: A polite, somewhat formal way to ask for information: 询问价格, 询问情况, 向…询问. It is not for a casual question; for that, plain 问.
column6: Tā xúnwèn le jiàgé.
column7: He asked about the price.
column9: A polite, somewhat formal way to ask for information: 詢問價格, 詢問情況, 向…詢問. It is not for a casual question; for that, plain 問.

column3: Takes a direct object or a clause: 猜对了, 猜谜语, 你猜他多大. Doubled, 猜猜 or 猜猜看, it invites a guess. 猜拳 is rock-paper-scissors.
column6: Nǐ cāi tā jīnnián duō dà?
column7: How old do you guess he is?
column9: Takes a direct object or a clause: 猜對了, 猜謎語, 你猜他多大. Doubled, 猜猜 or 猜猜看, it invites a guess. 猜拳 is rock-paper-scissors.

column3: The more formal, written 'guess' or speculation, both noun and verb: 我的猜测, 各种猜测, 猜测原因. The everyday word is 猜 (你猜猜看).
column6: Zhè zhǐshì wǒ de cāicè.
column7: This is only my guess.
column9: The more formal, written 'guess' or speculation, both noun and verb: 我的猜測, 各種猜測, 猜測原因. The everyday word is 猜 (你猜猜看).

column3: The wording of a slogan, whether shouted or printed: 喊口号, 宣传口号, 奥运口号. 标语 is the written banner or sign that carries one; an advertising slogan is usually 广告语.
column6: Dàjiā yīqǐ hǎn kǒuhào.
column7: Everyone shouted the slogan together.
column9: The wording of a slogan, whether shouted or printed: 喊口號, 宣傳口號, 奧運口號. 標語 is the written banner or sign that carries one; an advertising slogan is usually 廣告語.

column3: A way of putting something, and also a version or claim: 另一种说法, 官方说法. 给个说法 or 讨说法 means to give or demand an explanation owed after something went wrong.
column6: Zhè zhǒng shuōfa bù tài zhǔnquè.
column7: This way of putting it is not very accurate.
column9: A way of putting something, and also a version or claim: 另一種說法, 官方說法. 給個說法 or 討說法 means to give or demand an explanation owed after something went wrong.

column3: Written. What a person says, often with a judgment on tone: 言语粗鲁, 言语不当. Don't flip it: 语言 is 'language', while 言语 is the words someone speaks.
column4: 他言语粗鲁，让人很生气。
column5: 他言語粗魯，讓人很生氣。
column6: Tā yányǔ cūlǔ, ràng rén hěn shēngqì.
column7: His rude way of speaking made people angry.
column9: Written. What a person says, often with a judgment on tone: 言語粗魯, 言語不當. Don't flip it: 語言 is 'language', while 言語 is the words someone speaks.

column3: The Chinese language, as Chinese people overseas, especially in Singapore and Malaysia, call it: 说华语 "speak Chinese", 华语教学 "Chinese teaching", 华语电影 "Chinese-language films". In Taiwan it is a name for Mandarin, as in 华语文. In mainland China people say 汉语 or 普通话. 华 is "China, Chinese" and 语 "language".
column6: Tā huì shuō Huáyǔ.
column7: He can speak Chinese.
column9: The Chinese language, as Chinese people overseas, especially in Singapore and Malaysia, call it: 說華語 "speak Chinese", 華語教學 "Chinese teaching", 華語電影 "Chinese-language films". In Taiwan it is a name for Mandarin, as in 華語文. In mainland China people say 漢語 or 普通話. 華 is "China, Chinese" and 語 "language".

column3: Relays a message, order or feeling from one party to another, often down from above: 传达消息, 传达精神. Not the same as 表达, expressing your own thoughts. 传达室 is the gatehouse at the entrance of a school, office or compound.
column4: 请把这个消息传达给大家。
column5: 請把這個消息傳達給大家。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhège xiāoxi chuándá gěi dàjiā.
column7: Please pass this news on to everyone.
column9: Relays a message, order or feeling from one party to another, often down from above: 傳達消息, 傳達精神. Not the same as 表達, expressing your own thoughts. 傳達室 is the gatehouse at the entrance of a school, office or compound.

column3: Both noun and verb: 产生误解, 消除误解, 误解了他. Used for ideas as well as people. For a misunderstanding between people in speech, 误会 is the usual word (你误会了).
column6: Zhè shì yī ge wùjiě.
column7: This is a misunderstanding.
column9: Both noun and verb: 產生誤解, 消除誤解, 誤解了他. Used for ideas as well as people. For a misunderstanding between people in speech, 誤會 is the usual word (你誤會了).

column3: Three common uses: to instruct (交代工作), to hand over (交代给接班人), and to account for or confess (交代清楚, 交代罪行). 给…一个交代 means to give an explanation owed to someone.
column4: 老师交代了明天的作业。
column5: 老師交代了明天的作業。
column6: Lǎoshī jiāodài le míngtiān de zuòyè.
column7: The teacher gave instructions about tomorrow's homework.
column9: Three common uses: to instruct (交代工作), to hand over (交代給接班人), and to account for or confess (交代清楚, 交代罪行). 給…一個交代 means to give an explanation owed to someone.

column3: A field of study as a whole: 基础学科, 跨学科. For a subject on a timetable or an exam, 科目 or 课 is the usual word; 学科 is the academic field behind it.
column4: 计算机科学是一门新兴学科。
column5: 計算機科學是一門新興學科。
column6: Jìsuànjī kēxué shì yī mén xīnxīng xuékē.
column7: Computer science is a new academic field.
column9: A field of study as a whole: 基礎學科, 跨學科. For a subject on a timetable or an exam, 科目 or 課 is the usual word; 學科 is the academic field behind it.

column3: Taken by choice, the opposite of 必修: 选修课, 选修一门法语. A standard word at Chinese schools and universities. 修 here means to study a course.
column6: Wǒ xuǎnxiū le yī mén Fǎyǔ kè.
column7: I took a French course as an elective.
column9: Taken by choice, the opposite of 必修: 選修課, 選修一門法語. A standard word at Chinese schools and universities. 修 here means to study a course.

column3: A topic being researched or a problem to tackle, in universities and policy: 研究课题, 课题组, 新课题. It is not a class topic; for the topic of a talk or essay, say 题目.
column6: Zhège kètí hěn yǒu yìsi.
column7: This research topic is very interesting.
column9: A topic being researched or a problem to tackle, in universities and policy: 研究課題, 課題組, 新課題. It is not a class topic; for the topic of a talk or essay, say 題目.

column3: Learning the basics of a subject: 入门书, 入门级, 刚入门. A separable verb, so 入了门 and 入不了门 work. As a modifier it means beginner level.
column6: Zhè běn shū shìhé rùmén.
column7: This book suits beginners.
column9: Learning the basics of a subject: 入門書, 入門級, 剛入門. A separable verb, so 入了門 and 入不了門 work. As a modifier it means beginner level.

column3: Familiar through experience or time spent: 熟悉环境, 对…很熟悉; the opposite is 陌生. 了解 is to understand something, 熟悉 to know it well from use.
column6: Wǒ duì zhège chéngshì hěn shúxī.
column7: I know this city very well.
column9: Familiar through experience or time spent: 熟悉環境, 對…很熟悉; the opposite is 陌生. 了解 is to understand something, 熟悉 to know it well from use.

column3: With a skill or knowledge, it means knowing it well enough to use it: 掌握技术, 熟练掌握. With power or a situation, it means control: 掌握情况, 掌握命运.
column4: 他已经掌握了这门技术。
column5: 他已經掌握了這門技術。
column6: Tā yǐjīng zhǎngwò le zhè mén jìshù.
column7: He has already mastered this skill.
column9: With a skill or knowledge, it means knowing it well enough to use it: 掌握技術, 熟練掌握. With power or a situation, it means control: 掌握情況, 掌握命運.

column3: Noun and verb. A particular memory (童年的记忆) or the ability to remember (记忆力). 回忆 is the act of going back over memories; 记性 is the colloquial word for how good your memory is.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ tóngnián de jìyì.
column7: This is a memory from my childhood.
column9: Noun and verb. A particular memory (童年的記憶) or the ability to remember (記憶力). 回憶 is the act of going back over memories; 記性 is the colloquial word for how good your memory is.

column3: Going back over the past: 回忆往事, 回忆起. As a noun, memories of any kind: 美好的回忆, 痛苦的回忆. Unlike 记忆, the memory itself, it is the act of recalling; 回忆录 is a memoir.
column6: Tā zài huíyì xiǎoshíhou de shì.
column7: He is remembering things from his childhood.
column9: Going back over the past: 回憶往事, 回憶起. As a noun, memories of any kind: 美好的回憶, 痛苦的回憶. Unlike 記憶, the memory itself, it is the act of recalling; 回憶錄 is a memoir.

column3: Looks back to take stock of a period, event or career, usually in speeches and reports: 回顾历史, 回顾展. Unlike 回忆, which is personal memory, it reviews in order to learn from the past.
column4: 我们来回顾一下今年的工作。
column5: 我們來回顧一下今年的工作。
column6: Wǒmen lái huígù yīxià jīnnián de gōngzuò.
column7: Let's look back over this year's work.
column9: Looks back to take stock of a period, event or career, usually in speeches and reports: 回顧歷史, 回顧展. Unlike 回憶, which is personal memory, it reviews in order to learn from the past.

column3: Copies a person's voice, manner or style, often as a way to learn: 模仿大人说话, 模仿秀. 仿 alone marks imitation too: 仿古. A knockoff product is 仿冒, not 模仿.
column4: 孩子喜欢模仿大人说话。
column5: 孩子喜歡模仿大人說話。
column6: Háizi xǐhuan mófǎng dàrén shuōhuà.
column7: Children like to imitate how adults talk.
column9: Copies a person's voice, manner or style, often as a way to learn: 模仿大人說話, 模仿秀. 仿 alone marks imitation too: 仿古. A knockoff product is 仿冒, not 模仿.

column3: Showing how to do something by doing it yourself: 示范动作, 做示范. Unlike 演示, which shows a product or slides. Before a noun it means model or pilot: 示范学校, 示范区.
column4: 老师先给我们示范了一遍。
column5: 老師先給我們示範了一遍。
column6: Lǎoshī xiān gěi wǒmen shìfàn le yī biàn.
column7: The teacher first demonstrated it for us.
column9: Showing how to do something by doing it yourself: 示範動作, 做示範. Unlike 演示, which shows a product or slides. Before a noun it means model or pilot: 示範學校, 示範區.

column3: Both a verb and a noun: a teacher or a book 启发 someone, and the learner 受到启发 or 得到启发. It is about a new idea or insight, not excitement (that is 激励).
column4: 这本书给了我很多启发。
column5: 這本書給了我很多啟發。
column6: Zhè běn shū gěi le wǒ hěn duō qǐfā.
column7: This book gave me a lot of inspiration.
column9: Both a verb and a noun: a teacher or a book 啟發 someone, and the learner 受到啟發 or 得到啟發. It is about a new idea or insight, not excitement (that is 激勵).

column3: Housing a school or company provides: 学生宿舍, 员工宿舍. The building is the 宿舍楼, your roommate is 室友, and you say 住在宿舍 or just 住宿舍.
column6: Wǒ de sùshè lí jiàoshì hěn jìn.
column7: My dormitory is very close to the classroom.
column9: Housing a school or company provides: 學生宿舍, 員工宿舍. The building is the 宿舍樓, your roommate is 室友, and you say 住在宿舍 or just 住宿舍.

column3: A learned, practical skill: 掌握技能, 职业技能, 技能培训. For natural gift, 才能 fits better, and 技术 is technology or technique.
column6: Tā yǒu hěn duō shēnghuó jìnéng.
column7: He has many practical life skills.
column9: A learned, practical skill: 掌握技能, 職業技能, 技能培訓. For natural gift, 才能 fits better, and 技術 is technology or technique.

column3: The levels are 学士, 硕士 and 博士学位 (bachelor, master, doctorate), and you 获得 or 读 one. 学历 is different: the level of schooling you have completed.
column6: Tā zài gōngdú bóshì xuéwèi.
column7: He is working toward a doctorate.
column9: The levels are 學士, 碩士 and 博士學位 (bachelor, master, doctorate), and you 獲得 or 讀 one. 學歷 is different: the level of schooling you have completed.

column3: For books, magazines and recordings: 出版社 is a publishing house, 出版物 a publication. An article or paper in a journal is 发表, not 出版.
column6: Zhè běn shū qùnián chūbǎn le.
column7: This book was published last year.
column9: For books, magazines and recordings: 出版社 is a publishing house, 出版物 a publication. An article or paper in a journal is 發表, not 出版.

column3: Mostly met in compounds: 头版 front page, 版本 version, 盗版 pirated, 英文版 English edition. Editions are numbered with it: 第二版.
column6: Zhè běn shū chū le xīn bǎn.
column7: A new edition of this book has come out.
column9: Mostly met in compounds: 頭版 front page, 版本 version, 盜版 pirated, 英文版 English edition. Editions are numbered with it: 第二版.

column3: Says an item is the licensed one, not a copy: 正版软件, 正版书, 买正版, 支持正版. The opposite is 盗版, pirated. Used for software, books, films, music and games.
column6: Wǒ zhǐ mǎi zhèngbǎn shū.
column7: I only buy books that aren’t pirated.
column9: Says an item is the licensed one, not a copy: 正版軟件, 正版書, 買正版, 支持正版. The opposite is 盜版, pirated. Used for software, books, films, music and games.

column3: X版 names a form or edition: 电子版 (a file), 纸质版 (print), 中文版, 手机版. You ask 有电子版吗？ when you want a digital copy of a book or document.
column6: Wǒ yǒu zhè běn shū de diànzǐbǎn.
column7: I have an electronic version of this book.
column9: X版 names a form or edition: 電子版 (a file), 紙質版 (print), 中文版, 手機版. You ask 有電子版嗎？ when you want a digital copy of a book or document.

column3: Printing as production: 印刷厂 a print shop, 印刷品 printed matter, 印刷术 the technique. Printing a file from your computer is a different word: 打印 on the mainland, 列印 in Taiwan.
column6: Zhè běn shū yìnshuā de hěn qīngchu.
column7: This book is printed very clearly.
column9: Printing as production: 印刷廠 a print shop, 印刷品 printed matter, 印刷術 the technique. Printing a file from your computer is a different word: 打印 on the mainland, 列印 in Taiwan.

column3: The same word is the action and the job: 编辑文章 edit an article, 责任编辑 the editor in charge. In software menus it is the Edit command.
column6: Tā zài chūbǎnshè dāng biānjí.
column7: She works as an editor at a publishing house.
column9: The same word is the action and the job: 編輯文章 edit an article, 責任編輯 the editor in charge. In software menus it is the Edit command.

column3: Strictly a dictionary of words and phrases, but in speech 字典 is used for any dictionary (查字典). 词典 is the usual wording on the mainland, 辞典 the one common in Taiwan.
column6: Zhè běn cídiǎn hěn hǎoyòng.
column7: This dictionary is very useful.
column9: Strictly a dictionary of words and phrases, but in speech 字典 is used for any dictionary (查字典). 詞典 is the usual wording on the mainland, 辭典 the one common in Taiwan.

column3: Prose, and especially the essay as a literary form: 写散文 "write essays", 散文集 "a collection of essays", 散文诗 "prose poem", 散文家 "essayist". In Chinese literature it is a form of its own, free in structure, covering essays, sketches and reflections, and it does not mean "novels". 散 is read sǎn here, "loose", not sàn.
column6: Tā xiě le yī piān sǎnwén.
column7: He wrote an essay.
column9: Prose, and especially the essay as a literary form: 寫散文 "write essays", 散文集 "a collection of essays", 散文詩 "prose poem", 散文家 "essayist". In Chinese literature it is a form of its own, free in structure, covering essays, sketches and reflections, and it does not mean "novels". 散 is read sǎn here, "loose", not sàn.

column3: The general term for poetry as a genre: 现代诗歌, 诗歌朗诵, 喜欢诗歌. A single poem is usually just 诗, counted with 首: 一首诗.
column6: Tā xǐhuan dú xiàndài shīgē.
column7: She likes reading modern poetry.
column9: The general term for poetry as a genre: 現代詩歌, 詩歌朗誦, 喜歡詩歌. A single poem is usually just 詩, counted with 首: 一首詩.

column3: A set phrase, mostly of four characters, tied to a story or classical text, so its meaning is often not the sum of its characters: 画蛇添足 ("add feet to a snake") means spoiling things by overdoing them.
column6: Zhège chéngyǔ shì shénme yìsi?
column7: What does this idiom mean?
column9: A set phrase, mostly of four characters, tied to a story or classical text, so its meaning is often not the sum of its characters: 畫蛇添足 ("add feet to a snake") means spoiling things by overdoing them.

column3: The kind of subject a work takes up: 历史题材, 现实题材, for films, novels, paintings. Not the same as 主题, the central message or theme the work is about.
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng de tícái hěn xīn.
column7: The subject of this film is very fresh.
column9: The kind of subject a work takes up: 歷史題材, 現實題材, for films, novels, paintings. Not the same as 主題, the central message or theme the work is about.

column3: The sequence of events in a story, film or game: 情节复杂, 情节简单, 情节发展. In law and news it means the circumstances of a case: 情节严重.
column4: 这个故事的情节很复杂。
column5: 這個故事的情節很複雜。
column6: Zhège gùshi de qíngjié hěn fùzá.
column7: The plot of this story is very complicated.
column9: The sequence of events in a story, film or game: 情節複雜, 情節簡單, 情節發展. In law and news it means the circumstances of a case: 情節嚴重.

column3: The art of writing with a brush, also a school subject: 练书法, 毛笔书法, 书法家. Ordinary handwriting is 字: 他的字写得很好.
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo liànxí shūfǎ.
column7: He has practiced calligraphy since he was little.
column9: The art of writing with a brush, also a school subject: 練書法, 毛筆書法, 書法家. Ordinary handwriting is 字: 他的字寫得很好.

column3: Literature and the arts together, often in the name of an event: 文艺晚会, 文艺演出. As a spoken adjective it means artsy: 文艺青年, 很文艺.
column6: Tā xǐhuan wényì huódòng.
column7: She likes cultural events.
column9: Literature and the arts together, often in the name of an event: 文藝晚會, 文藝演出. As a spoken adjective it means artsy: 文藝青年, 很文藝.

column3: Counted with 架: 一架钢琴. You 弹 it, 练 it or 学 it. Words ending in 琴 are instruments in general: 小提琴 violin, 手风琴 accordion.
column4: 她每天练一个小时钢琴。
column5: 她每天練一個小時鋼琴。
column6: Tā měitiān liàn yī ge xiǎoshí gāngqín.
column7: She practices the piano for an hour every day.
column9: Counted with 架: 一架鋼琴. You 彈 it, 練 it or 學 it. Words ending in 琴 are instruments in general: 小提琴 violin, 手風琴 accordion.

column3: A stringed instrument. Used in names of many instruments: 钢琴 "piano", 小提琴 "violin", 古琴 (the zither), 口琴 "harmonica". On its own, 拉琴 is "play a bowed instrument" and 弹琴 "play one plucked with the fingers, or with keys". Two strings 玨 on top and 今 for the sound.
column6: Tā huì lā qín.
column7: She can play a bowed instrument.
column9: A stringed instrument. Used in names of many instruments: 鋼琴 "piano", 小提琴 "violin", 古琴 (the zither), 口琴 "harmonica". On its own, 拉琴 is "play a bowed instrument" and 彈琴 "play one plucked with the fingers, or with keys". Two strings 玨 on top and 今 for the sound.

column3: A song as a piece of music: 流行歌曲, 一首歌曲. In speech people say 歌: 唱歌, 听歌, 这首歌好听. 歌曲 is the more formal choice. 曲 is read qǔ here, meaning a tune.
column6: Zhè shǒu gēqǔ hěn hǎotīng.
column7: This song sounds lovely.
column9: A song as a piece of music: 流行歌曲, 一首歌曲. In speech people say 歌: 唱歌, 聽歌, 這首歌好聽. 歌曲 is the more formal choice. 曲 is read qǔ here, meaning a tune.

column3: Counted with 张: 一张专辑. To release one is 出专辑 or 发行专辑. 专 means focused on one thing, so a 专辑 gathers one artist's or one theme's work.
column4: 这位歌手出了一张新专辑。
column5: 這位歌手出了一張新專輯。
column6: Zhè wèi gēshǒu chū le yī zhāng xīn zhuānjí.
column7: This singer has released a new album.
column9: Counted with 張: 一張專輯. To release one is 出專輯 or 發行專輯. 專 means focused on one thing, so a 專輯 gathers one artist's or one theme's work.

column3: In speech you 跳舞 or 跳一支舞; alone as a verb it is literary (载歌载舞). It starts many words: 舞台 stage, 舞会 dance party, 舞蹈 dance as an art. The character was coined to keep the original meaning of its top part, "dancing".
column6: Tā de wǔ tiào de hěn hǎo.
column7: She dances very well.
column9: In speech you 跳舞 or 跳一支舞; alone as a verb it is literary (載歌載舞). It starts many words: 舞臺 stage, 舞會 dance party, 舞蹈 dance as an art. The character was coined to keep the original meaning of its top part, "dancing".

column3: Stage drama, especially opera, in speech: 看戏, 唱戏, counted with 出: 一出戏. Figurative uses: 没戏 means no chance, and 演戏 can mean putting on an act.
column6: Zhè chū xì hěn hǎokàn.
column7: This play is very good to watch.
column9: Stage drama, especially opera, in speech: 看戲, 唱戲, counted with 出: 一出戲. Figurative uses: 沒戲 means no chance, and 演戲 can mean putting on an act.

column3: Drama as an art or a field of study, covering spoken plays and opera: 戏剧节, 学戏剧. One show is 一出戏, a spoken play 话剧. 戏剧性 means dramatic: 戏剧性的变化.
column6: Tā zài dàxué xuéxí xìjù.
column7: He studies drama at university.
column9: Drama as an art or a field of study, covering spoken plays and opera: 戲劇節, 學戲劇. One show is 一出戲, a spoken play 話劇. 戲劇性 means dramatic: 戲劇性的變化.

column3: Comedy as a genre: 喜剧片, 喜剧演员; the opposite is 悲剧. 剧 ends many genre words: 电视剧 TV series, 歌剧 opera, 话剧 spoken drama.
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn xǐjù diànyǐng.
column7: I like watching comedy films.
column9: Comedy as a genre: 喜劇片, 喜劇演員; the opposite is 悲劇. 劇 ends many genre words: 電視劇 TV series, 歌劇 opera, 話劇 spoken drama.

column3: It needs the part as its object (扮演老师, 扮演重要角色), on stage or in real life. 演 is looser: you can 演戏 or 演电影 without naming a part.
column4: 她在电影里扮演一位老师。
column5: 她在電影裡扮演一位老師。
column6: Tā zài diànyǐng lǐ bànyǎn yī wèi lǎoshī.
column7: She plays a teacher in the film.
column9: It needs the part as its object (扮演老師, 扮演重要角色), on stage or in real life. 演 is looser: you can 演戲 or 演電影 without naming a part.

column3: Crosstalk, a comic dialogue between two performers: 说相声 "perform crosstalk", 听相声, 相声演员. A traditional northern art, with fast jokes and wordplay, and now often heard on stage and online. 声 is neutral here, though it is shēng by itself. 相 is read xiàng here, "mutual, a pair".
column6: Tā xǐhuan tīng xiàngsheng.
column7: He likes listening to crosstalk.
column9: Crosstalk, a comic dialogue between two performers: 說相聲 "perform crosstalk", 聽相聲, 相聲演員. A traditional northern art, with fast jokes and wordplay, and now often heard on stage and online. 聲 is neutral here, though it is shēng by itself. 相 is read xiàng here, "mutual, a pair".

column3: The written text of a play or film: 写剧本, 改编剧本. The writer is 编剧, and the actors' lines are 台词. 剧本杀 is a murder-mystery party game.
column6: Tā zhèngzài xiě yī ge jùběn.
column7: He is writing a script.
column9: The written text of a play or film: 寫劇本, 改編劇本. The writer is 編劇, and the actors' lines are 臺詞. 劇本殺 is a murder-mystery party game.

column3: Three verb uses: to beat (鼓掌 applaud), to rouse (鼓励 encourage, 鼓起勇气 summon up courage) and to bulge (腮帮子鼓鼓的 puffed-out cheeks). It combines a drum with a hand holding a drumstick.
column6: Háizi zài qiāo gǔ.
column7: The child is beating a drum.
column9: Three verb uses: to beat (鼓掌 applaud), to rouse (鼓勵 encourage, 鼓起勇氣 summon up courage) and to bulge (腮幫子鼓鼓的 puffed-out cheeks). It combines a drum with a hand holding a drumstick.

column3: Sound, voice, tone: 声音 "sound", 大声 "loudly", 声调 "tone", 名声 "reputation", 声明 "statement". As a measure word it counts sounds and cries: 一声 "one cry", 叫了两声, said yìshēng. In names of the tones, 一声 is first tone, said yīshēng. On its own, it is the measure; the noun 声音 is more common for "sound".
column6: Wǒ tīngjiàn yī shēng jùxiǎng.
column7: I heard a loud bang.
column9: Sound, voice, tone: 聲音 "sound", 大聲 "loudly", 聲調 "tone", 名聲 "reputation", 聲明 "statement". As a measure word it counts sounds and cries: 一聲 "one cry", 叫了兩聲, said yìshēng. In names of the tones, 一聲 is first tone, said yīshēng. On its own, it is the measure; the noun 聲音 is more common for "sound".

column3: Photography as an art or hobby: 摄影师, 摄影展, 爱好摄影. Taking one picture is 拍照. In film credits, 摄影 is the cinematography.
column6: Tā xǐhuan shèyǐng.
column7: He likes photography.
column9: Photography as an art or hobby: 攝影師, 攝影展, 愛好攝影. Taking one picture is 拍照. In film credits, 攝影 is the cinematography.

column3: 师 turns a craft into the person who does it: 设计师 designer, 律师 lawyer, 化妆师 makeup artist. This one is a photographer, and on a film crew the cinematographer.
column6: Shèyǐngshī zhèngzài pāizhào.
column7: The photographer is taking pictures.
column9: 師 turns a craft into the person who does it: 設計師 designer, 律師 lawyer, 化妝師 makeup artist. This one is a photographer, and on a film crew the cinematographer.

column3: Video, as against still photos (摄影). Everyday mainland speech says 拍视频 or 录像; 摄像 shows up in 摄像头, a small camera built into a phone or laptop or fixed on a wall (the lens itself is 镜头). Taiwan says 录影 or 拍影片 for recording video, and 镜头 or 摄影机 where the mainland says 摄像头.
column6: Zhè bù shǒujī kěyǐ shèxiàng.
column7: This phone can record video.
column9: Video, as against still photos (攝影). Everyday mainland speech says 拍視頻 or 錄像; 攝像 shows up in 攝像頭, a small camera built into a phone or laptop or fixed on a wall (the lens itself is 鏡頭). Taiwan says 錄影 or 拍影片 for recording video, and 鏡頭 or 攝影機 where the mainland says 攝像頭.

column3: 机 ends words for machines and aircraft: 照相机 camera, 收音机 radio, 飞机 plane. Counted with 台. 摄像机 is a stand-alone video camera; 摄像头 is any small camera module (phone, laptop, CCTV). Taiwan says 摄影机 for the video camera, and 监视器 for a security camera.
column6: Tā mǎi le yī tái shèxiàngjī.
column7: He bought a video camera.
column9: 機 ends words for machines and aircraft: 照相機 camera, 收音機 radio, 飛機 plane. Counted with 臺. 攝像機 is a stand-alone video camera; 攝像頭 is any small camera module (phone, laptop, CCTV). Taiwan says 攝影機 for the video camera, and 監視器 for a security camera.

column3: More formal than 拍, the everyday verb (拍照, 拍视频, 拍电影). 拍摄 turns up in credits and news: 拍摄现场 the filming location, 在北京拍摄.
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng zài Běijīng pāishè.
column7: This film was shot in Beijing.
column9: More formal than 拍, the everyday verb (拍照, 拍視頻, 拍電影). 拍攝 turns up in credits and news: 拍攝現場 the filming location, 在北京拍攝.

column3: Used to judge how a picture looks: 画面清晰, 画面很美, 画面模糊. 图片 is a still image; 画面 is what is displayed in a frame or on a screen.
column6: Diànyǐng de huàmiàn hěn měi.
column7: The pictures in the film are beautiful.
column9: Used to judge how a picture looks: 畫面清晰, 畫面很美, 畫面模糊. 圖片 is a still image; 畫面 is what is displayed in a frame or on a screen.

column3: Comics for reading: 看漫画, 漫画书, 漫画家, 日本漫画. Animation is 动画, and 动漫 covers both animation and comics.
column6: Háizi xǐhuan kàn mànhuà.
column7: Children like to read comics.
column9: Comics for reading: 看漫畫, 漫畫書, 漫畫家, 日本漫畫. Animation is 動畫, and 動漫 covers both animation and comics.

column3: Verb and noun: 举办展览 hold one, 参观展览 visit one. The venue is a 展览馆; a trade fair or expo is usually a 展会. Showing one thing to someone is 展示.
column6: Zhège zhǎnlǎn hěn shòu huānyíng.
column7: This exhibition is very popular.
column9: Verb and noun: 舉辦展覽 hold one, 參觀展覽 visit one. The venue is a 展覽館; a trade fair or expo is usually a 展會. Showing one thing to someone is 展示.

column3: For presenting something on purpose: 展示成果, 展示才华, 向大家展示. Plain "show me" in speech is 给我看, and 展览 is the exhibition itself.
column4: 他向大家展示了新产品。
column5: 他向大家展示了新產品。
column6: Tā xiàng dàjiā zhǎnshì le xīn chǎnpǐn.
column7: He showed everyone the new product.
column9: For presenting something on purpose: 展示成果, 展示才華, 向大家展示. Plain "show me" in speech is 給我看, and 展覽 is the exhibition itself.

column3: A sight meeting the eye, often lively or moving: 热闹的景象, 繁荣景象. It suits scenes with people and activity; natural scenery is 风景.
column6: Yǎnqián de jǐngxiàng ràng rén nánwàng.
column7: The sight before our eyes was unforgettable.
column9: A sight meeting the eye, often lively or moving: 熱鬧的景象, 繁榮景象. It suits scenes with people and activity; natural scenery is 風景.

column3: Scenery with a place before it, as in travel writing: 田园风光, 江南风光; 风景 is the everyday word. It also describes people doing well and looked up to: 他现在很风光.
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngguāng hěn měi.
column7: The scenery here is very beautiful.
column9: Scenery with a place before it, as in travel writing: 田園風光, 江南風光; 風景 is the everyday word. It also describes people doing well and looked up to: 他現在很風光.

column3: A craft or the way something is made: 传统工艺, 工艺品 handicrafts. In factories it means the manufacturing process: 生产工艺, 工艺流程.
column6: Zhè shì yī zhǒng chuántǒng gōngyì.
column7: This is a traditional craft.
column9: A craft or the way something is made: 傳統工藝, 工藝品 handicrafts. In factories it means the manufacturing process: 生產工藝, 工藝流程.

column3: Something shows itself, usually a quality or a scene: 展现魅力, 展现出美丽, 展现在眼前. 展示 is a deliberate presenting; 展现 reveals.
column4: 这幅画展现了乡村的美。
column5: 這幅畫展現了鄉村的美。
column6: Zhè fú huà zhǎnxiàn le xiāngcūn de měi.
column7: This painting shows the beauty of the countryside.
column9: Something shows itself, usually a quality or a scene: 展現魅力, 展現出美麗, 展現在眼前. 展示 is a deliberate presenting; 展現 reveals.

column3: Mostly a building block: 显得 seem, 明显 obvious, 显然 clearly, 显示 display. On its own it is everyday for how something makes you look: 显瘦, 显老, 显年轻.
column6: Zhè tiáo kùzi hěn xiǎn shòu.
column7: These pants make you look slim.
column9: Mostly a building block: 顯得 seem, 明顯 obvious, 顯然 clearly, 顯示 display. On its own it is everyday for how something makes you look: 顯瘦, 顯老, 顯年輕.

column3: Both the sport and the shuttlecock. Racket and hand sports take 打: 打羽毛球, 打乒乓球, 打篮球; soccer (足球) takes 踢. The racket is the 羽毛球拍.
column6: Wǒmen zhōumò dǎ yǔmáoqiú.
column7: We play badminton on weekends.
column9: Both the sport and the shuttlecock. Racket and hand sports take 打: 打羽毛球, 打乒乓球, 打籃球; soccer (足球) takes 踢. The racket is the 羽毛球拍.

column3: In sport the person is the referee or umpire, who 吹哨子; in law the word is the act of ruling: 法院裁判. A court judge is a 法官. 裁 also means to cut back, e.g. on staff, as well as a decision or judgment.
column6: Cáipàn chuī le shàozi.
column7: The referee blew the whistle.
column9: In sport the person is the referee or umpire, who 吹哨子; in law the word is the act of ruling: 法院裁判. A court judge is a 法官. 裁 also means to cut back, e.g. on staff, as well as a decision or judgment.

column3: Used for the winner of a contest: 世界冠军, 拿冠军, 冠军赛. Second place is 亚军 and third 季军. 冠 is read guàn when it means being first, as here, and guān for a hat.
column6: Tā dé le yóuyǒng guànjūn.
column7: She won the swimming championship.
column9: Used for the winner of a contest: 世界冠軍, 拿冠軍, 冠軍賽. Second place is 亞軍 and third 季軍. 冠 is read guàn when it means being first, as here, and guān for a hat.

column3: The runner-up. The ranking words all end in 军: 冠军 first, 亚军 second, 季军 third. In Taiwan 亚 is commonly read yǎ, both for second and for Asia.
column6: Wǒmen duì dé le yàjūn.
column7: Our team came second.
column9: The runner-up. The ranking words all end in 軍: 冠軍 first, 亞軍 second, 季軍 third. In Taiwan 亞 is commonly read yǎ, both for second and for Asia.

column3: A formal contest with rules, often in school subjects or work: 数学竞赛, 知识竞赛. 比赛 is the everyday word for a match or game.
column6: Xuéxiào jǔbàn le shùxué jìngsài.
column7: The school held a math competition.
column9: A formal contest with rules, often in school subjects or work: 數學競賽, 知識競賽. 比賽 is the everyday word for a match or game.

column3: 赛 ends names of contests: 比赛, 决赛, 联赛. 大奖赛 is how "Grand Prix" is rendered, as in Formula One, and it names any contest with major prizes, like a piano competition.
column6: Tā cānjiā le guójì dàjiǎngsài.
column7: He took part in the international grand prix.
column9: 賽 ends names of contests: 比賽, 決賽, 聯賽. 大獎賽 is how "Grand Prix" is rendered, as in Formula One, and it names any contest with major prizes, like a piano competition.

column3: Opposites joined into one noun, like 大小 size or 长短 length: 胜负 is the outcome. Typical: 决定胜负, 分出胜负, 胜负未分 undecided.
column6: Bǐsài de shèngfù hái hěn nán shuō.
column7: It is still hard to say who will win the match.
column9: Opposites joined into one noun, like 大小 size or 長短 length: 勝負 is the outcome. Typical: 決定勝負, 分出勝負, 勝負未分 undecided.

column3: For events open to the public: exhibitions, conferences, festivals, games. The opposite is 闭幕. 幕 also counts the acts of a play: 第一幕. A shop opening for business is 开业 on the mainland, while in Taiwan 开幕 is the ordinary word for it.
column6: Zhǎnlǎn míngtiān kāimù.
column7: The exhibition opens tomorrow.
column9: For events open to the public: exhibitions, conferences, festivals, games. The opposite is 閉幕. 幕 also counts the acts of a play: 第一幕. A shop opening for business is 開業 on the mainland, while in Taiwan 開幕 is the ordinary word for it.

column3: In ceremony names 式 follows the occasion: 开幕式, 闭幕式. The same 式 means style or type in 中式, 西式, 日式 (Chinese-, Western-, Japanese-style).
column4: 开幕式在晚上八点开始。
column5: 開幕式在晚上八點開始。
column6: Kāimùshì zài wǎnshang bā diǎn kāishǐ.
column7: The opening ceremony starts at eight in the evening.
column9: In ceremony names 式 follows the occasion: 開幕式, 閉幕式. The same 式 means style or type in 中式, 西式, 日式 (Chinese-, Western-, Japanese-style).

column3: Said of events with a program, such as a meeting, festival, games or exhibition, and the event is the subject: 展览会今天闭幕. Its opposite is 开幕.
column6: Yùndònghuì zuótiān bìmù le.
column7: The games closed yesterday.
column9: Said of events with a program, such as a meeting, festival, games or exhibition, and the event is the subject: 展覽會今天閉幕. Its opposite is 開幕.

column3: The opening ceremony is 开幕式. Few events take 式 freely: other ceremonies are 典礼 or 仪式, as in 毕业典礼.
column6: Bìmùshì fēicháng jīngcǎi.
column7: The closing ceremony was wonderful.
column9: The opening ceremony is 開幕式. Few events take 式 freely: other ceremonies are 典禮 or 儀式, as in 畢業典禮.

column3: A big, formal occasion with speeches, held by schools and institutions: 毕业典礼, 开学典礼. A wedding is usually 婚礼, and 仪式 is the plainer word for any ritual.
column6: Bìyè diǎnlǐ zài lǐtáng jǔxíng.
column7: The graduation ceremony is held in the hall.
column9: A big, formal occasion with speeches, held by schools and institutions: 畢業典禮, 開學典禮. A wedding is usually 婚禮, and 儀式 is the plainer word for any ritual.

column3: Both a verb and a noun, for companies, jobs and markets: 竞争对手, 竞争力, 公平竞争. 竞争 is the rivalry itself; 比赛 is an organized contest with rules and a winner.
column4: 公司之间的竞争很激烈。
column5: 公司之間的競爭很激烈。
column6: Gōngsī zhījiān de jìngzhēng hěn jīliè.
column7: The competition between companies is fierce.
column9: Both a verb and a noun, for companies, jobs and markets: 競爭對手, 競爭力, 公平競爭. 競爭 is the rivalry itself; 比賽 is an organized contest with rules and a winner.

column3: A verb and a noun, for a reward meant to encourage good results: 物质奖励, 奖励制度. To win a prize is 获奖 or 得奖, and its opposite in spirit is 惩罚.
column6: Lǎoshī jiǎnglì le tā yī běn shū.
column7: The teacher rewarded him with a book.
column9: A verb and a noun, for a reward meant to encourage good results: 物質獎勵, 獎勵制度. To win a prize is 獲獎 or 得獎, and its opposite in spirit is 懲罰.

column3: Two common senses: putting pieces together (拼图, 拼车, 拼音) and going all out for a goal (拼命, 拼搏). The second is typical of encouragement: 拼一把, 拼了.
column6: Wǒmen yào pīn dào zuìhòu.
column7: We must fight until the end.
column9: Two common senses: putting pieces together (拼圖, 拼車, 拼音) and going all out for a goal (拼命, 拼搏). The second is typical of encouragement: 拼一把, 拼了.

column3: Anything sent out in a line: arrows (射箭), a ball at goal (射门), light and rays (照射, 射线), and 发射 for launching a rocket. In the oracle bone script it was a bow 弓 and an arrow 矢; later the bow and arrow became 身 and the hand became 寸.
column6: Tā shè le sān jiàn.
column7: He shot three arrows.
column9: Anything sent out in a line: arrows (射箭), a ball at goal (射門), light and rays (照射, 射線), and 發射 for launching a rocket. In the oracle bone script it was a bow 弓 and an arrow 矢; later the bow and arrow became 身 and the hand became 寸.

column3: Firing a gun, in war or as a sport (an Olympic event): 射击比赛, 向目标射击. For arrows use 射箭, and for a shot at goal 射门.
column6: Tā zài liànxí shèjī.
column7: He is practicing shooting.
column9: Firing a gun, in war or as a sport (an Olympic event): 射擊比賽, 向目標射擊. For arrows use 射箭, and for a shot at goal 射門.

column3: Met as a key on a keyboard or a button on a device: 按键, 回车键, 空格键. In 关键 it means the crucial point, one of the most common words you will see.
column6: Qǐng àn zhège jiàn.
column7: Please press this key.
column9: Met as a key on a keyboard or a button on a device: 按鍵, 回車鍵, 空格鍵. In 關鍵 it means the crucial point, one of the most common words you will see.

column3: Used for a computer keyboard and a piano keyboard alike. To type on it is 敲键盘 or 打字.
column6: Wǒ de jiànpán huài le.
column7: My keyboard is broken.
column9: Used for a computer keyboard and a piano keyboard alike. To type on it is 敲鍵盤 or 打字.

column3: The computer mouse: 点击鼠标, 鼠标垫. In Taiwan it is 滑鼠. The animal is 老鼠, since 鼠 rarely stands alone.
column6: Qǐng yòng shǔbiāo diǎn yīxià zhèlǐ.
column7: Please click here with the mouse.
column9: The computer mouse: 點擊鼠標, 鼠標墊. In Taiwan it is 滑鼠. The animal is 老鼠, since 鼠 rarely stands alone.

column3: Programs and apps, with 硬件 as its pair: 安装软件, 办公软件. In Taiwan the pair is 软体 and 硬体.
column4: 这个软件可以免费下载。
column5: 這個軟件可以免費下載。
column6: Zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ miǎnfèi xiàzài.
column7: You can download this software for free.
column9: Programs and apps, with 硬件 as its pair: 安裝軟件, 辦公軟件. In Taiwan the pair is 軟體 and 硬體.

column3: Computer hardware, and also the facilities of a place such as a school (buildings, equipment) as against its 软件, meaning management and teaching quality. In Taiwan the computer term is 硬体.
column6: Zhè tái diànnǎo de yìngjiàn hěn hǎo.
column7: This computer has very good hardware.
column9: Computer hardware, and also the facilities of a place such as a school (buildings, equipment) as against its 軟件, meaning management and teaching quality. In Taiwan the computer term is 硬體.

column3: Covers factory robots, robot vacuums (扫地机器人) and chatbots (聊天机器人). The 机 is the machine one, as in 手机 and 飞机.
column6: Zhège jīqìrén huì shuōhuà.
column7: This robot can talk.
column9: Covers factory robots, robot vacuums (掃地機器人) and chatbots (聊天機器人). The 機 is the machine one, as in 手機 and 飛機.

column3: Used for nearly everything on the mainland: paying, adding a contact, opening a menu. Scanning it is 扫码, as in 扫码支付. In Taiwan it is usually called QR码.
column6: Qǐng sǎo yīxià zhège èrwéimǎ.
column7: Please scan this QR code.
column9: Used for nearly everything on the mainland: paying, adding a contact, opening a menu. Scanning it is 掃碼, as in 掃碼支付. In Taiwan it is usually called QR碼.

column3: A TV or radio channel, or a channel on a video platform: 换频道, 体育频道. A channel of communication or sales is 渠道 instead.
column6: Qǐng huàn yī ge píndào.
column7: Please change to another channel.
column9: A TV or radio channel, or a channel on a video platform: 換頻道, 體育頻道. A channel of communication or sales is 渠道 instead.

column3: Searching a body of data or a place: 搜索引擎, 搜索结果, and search parties for people. To look for one lost thing, use 找.
column4: 我在网上搜索了很多资料。
column5: 我在網上搜索了很多資料。
column6: Wǒ zài wǎngshàng sōusuǒ le hěn duō zīliào.
column7: I searched the internet for a lot of information.
column9: Searching a body of data or a place: 搜索引擎, 搜索結果, and search parties for people. To look for one lost thing, use 找.

column3: It also means the blogger. The 客 marks a kind of person, as in 黑客 hacker. Taiwan says 部落格.
column6: Tā měitiān dōu xiě bókè.
column7: He writes his blog every day.
column9: It also means the blogger. The 客 marks a kind of person, as in 黑客 hacker. Taiwan says 部落格.

column3: Nearly always the platform Weibo: 发微博, 刷微博. A post is counted with 条, as in 一条微博, and 博客 is where the 博 comes from.
column6: Tā gāng fā le yī tiáo wēibó.
column7: He just posted on Weibo.
column9: Nearly always the platform Weibo: 發微博, 刷微博. A post is counted with 條, as in 一條微博, and 博客 is where the 博 comes from.

column3: A video clip online or on a phone: 看视频, 发视频; a film at the cinema is 电影. The mainland call is 视频通话. In Taiwan a clip is usually 影片 and a video call is 视讯.
column6: Wǒmen yòng shìpín liáotiān ba.
column7: Let's chat by video.
column9: A video clip online or on a phone: 看視頻, 發視頻; a film at the cinema is 電影. The mainland call is 視頻通話. In Taiwan a clip is usually 影片 and a video call is 視訊.

column3: Users of an app, platform or service: 手机用户, 用户名, 用户体验. A shop customer is 顾客, and a business client is 客户.
column6: Zhège ruǎnjiàn yǒu hěn duō yònghù.
column7: This software has a lot of users.
column9: Users of an app, platform or service: 手機用戶, 用戶名, 用戶體驗. A shop customer is 顧客, and a business client is 客戶.

column3: A computer, program or machine sending out data or power: 输出结果, 输出功率; its opposite is 输入. In formal writing it also means exporting goods or labor, as in 劳务输出.
column4: 这个软件可以输出图片。
column5: 這個軟件可以輸出圖片。
column6: Zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ shūchū túpiàn.
column7: This software can export pictures.
column9: A computer, program or machine sending out data or power: 輸出結果, 輸出功率; its opposite is 輸入. In formal writing it also means exporting goods or labor, as in 勞務輸出.

column3: Used in speech for a quick online search: 搜一下, 搜一搜, 搜不到. In writing it sits in 搜索, 搜查 (search a place) and 搜集 (collect). The right-hand part 叟 is the original character for searching, depicting a hand holding a torch indoors.
column6: Nǐ zài wǎngshàng sōu yīxià ba.
column7: Search for it online.
column9: Used in speech for a quick online search: 搜一下, 搜一搜, 搜不到. In writing it sits in 搜索, 搜查 (search a place) and 蒐集 (collect). The right-hand part 叟 is the original character for searching, depicting a hand holding a torch indoors.

column3: On its own only in speech about a particular price: 这个价可以吗. Otherwise it sits inside words: 原价, 降价, 价值. The usual word for the price of an item is 价格 or 价钱.
column6: Zhège jià kěyǐ ma?
column7: Is this price all right?
column9: On its own only in speech about a particular price: 這個價可以嗎. Otherwise it sits inside words: 原價, 降價, 價值. The usual word for the price of an item is 價格 or 價錢.

column3: The general level of prices, as in the news: 物价上涨, 物价高, 稳定物价. For the price of one item, use 价格.
column6: Zhège chéngshì de wùjià hěn gāo.
column7: Prices in this city are very high.
column9: The general level of prices, as in the news: 物價上漲, 物價高, 穩定物價. For the price of one item, use 價格.

column3: The goods are the subject: 牛肉涨价了. Its opposite is 降价. It is a verb plus object, so you can say 涨了价 or give an amount, 涨了两块钱. A seller raising prices is also 涨价.
column6: Zuìjìn niúròu yòu zhǎngjià le.
column7: Beef has gone up in price again lately.
column9: The goods are the subject: 牛肉漲價了. Its opposite is 降價. It is a verb plus object, so you can say 漲了價 or give an amount, 漲了兩塊錢. A seller raising prices is also 漲價.

column3: Rises of prices, water and wages: 价格涨了, 水位涨了, 涨工资. The opposite for prices is 跌.
column6: Héshuǐ zhǎng de hěn kuài.
column7: The river is rising fast.
column9: Rises of prices, water and wages: 價格漲了, 水位漲了, 漲工資. The opposite for prices is 跌.

column3: A written word for rising prices, wages or water levels: 价格上涨, 房价上涨. It takes no object, and in speech you hear just 涨.
column6: Jīnnián fángjià shàngzhǎng le bù shǎo.
column7: House prices have gone up a lot this year.
column9: A written word for rising prices, wages or water levels: 價格上漲, 房價上漲. It takes no object, and in speech you hear just 漲.

column3: The price you pay in effort, loss or sacrifice, not in money: 付出代价, 以健康为代价. For an ordinary price, use 价格.
column4: 他为这个错误付出了很大的代价。
column5: 他為這個錯誤付出了很大的代價。
column6: Tā wèi zhège cuòwù fùchū le hěn dà de dàijià.
column7: He paid a heavy price for this mistake.
column9: The price you pay in effort, loss or sacrifice, not in money: 付出代價, 以健康為代價. For an ordinary price, use 價格.

column3: The everyday word for a business or deal, against formal 贸易 or 交易: 做买卖, 一笔大买卖. As verbs it is plain buying and selling: 买卖房子. Selling is explained as causing someone to buy.
column6: Tā zuò de shì xiǎo mǎimai.
column7: He runs a small business.
column9: The everyday word for a business or deal, against formal 貿易 or 交易: 做買賣, 一筆大買賣. As verbs it is plain buying and selling: 買賣房子. Selling is explained as causing someone to buy.

column3: Buying goods in quantity for a company, school or household: 采购员, 采购部, 采购设备, and 采购年货 before New Year. It is more businesslike than 买. 采 began as a hand picking from a tree.
column4: 公司要采购一批新电脑。
column5: 公司要採購一批新電腦。
column6: Gōngsī yào cǎigòu yī pī xīn diànnǎo.
column7: The company is going to buy a batch of new computers.
column9: Buying goods in quantity for a company, school or household: 採購員, 採購部, 採購設備, and 採購年貨 before New Year. It is more businesslike than 買. 採 began as a hand picking from a tree.

column3: Buying up, in two settings: an organization buying produce in bulk (收购粮食), and one company taking over another (被收购). It differs from 采购, buying for your own use.
column4: 这家公司被大公司收购了。
column5: 這家公司被大公司收購了。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī bèi dà gōngsī shōugòu le.
column7: This company was bought by a big company.
column9: Buying up, in two settings: an organization buying produce in bulk (收購糧食), and one company taking over another (被收購). It differs from 採購, buying for your own use.

column3: A deal is closed; the subject is the deal: 这笔生意成交了. Also 成交价 (the price paid) and 成交量 (trading volume); in a market a haggle ends with a shout of 成交.
column4: 经过谈判，这笔生意终于成交了。
column5: 經過談判，這筆生意終於成交了。
column6: Jīngguò tánpàn, zhè bǐ shēngyi zhōngyú chéngjiāo le.
column7: After negotiating, the deal was finally closed.
column9: A deal is closed; the subject is the deal: 這筆生意成交了. Also 成交價 (the price paid) and 成交量 (trading volume); in a market a haggle ends with a shout of 成交.

column3: The registered mark of a brand: 注册商标, 商标权. A brand itself is 品牌.
column6: Zhège shāngbiāo hěn yǒumíng.
column7: This trademark is very famous.
column9: The registered mark of a brand: 註冊商標, 商標權. A brand itself is 品牌.

column3: Rarely alone: it ends words for goods (食品, 商品, 礼品, 产品, 药品) and also means character (人品) and to taste (品茶, 品尝). It is the mouth 口 written three times, standing for various objects.
column6: Nǐ lái pǐn yī pǐn zhè bēi chá.
column7: Come and taste this tea.
column9: Rarely alone: it ends words for goods (食品, 商品, 禮品, 產品, 藥品) and also means character (人品) and to taste (品茶, 品嘗). It is the mouth 口 written three times, standing for various objects.

column3: Kinds of plants, animals or products: 新品种, 苹果品种, 品种多. For kinds in general, 种类. Elsewhere 种 is read zhòng and means to plant.
column6: Zhèlǐ yǒu hěn duō píngguǒ pǐnzhǒng.
column7: There are many varieties of apple here.
column9: Kinds of plants, animals or products: 新品種, 蘋果品種, 品種多. For kinds in general, 種類. Elsewhere 種 is read zhòng and means to plant.

column3: Used in law, business and news: 消费者权益, 保护消费者. 者 makes the person who does it, as in 读者 and 作者. A shopper in a shop is 顾客.
column6: Shāngdiàn yào ràng xiāofèizhě mǎnyì.
column7: Shops have to satisfy their consumers.
column9: Used in law, business and news: 消費者權益, 保護消費者. 者 makes the person who does it, as in 讀者 and 作者. A shopper in a shop is 顧客.

column3: A business client or account: 重要客户, 客户服务, 接待客户. A shopper in a store is 顾客. A client program or app is 客户端.
column4: 我今天要见一个重要的客户。
column5: 我今天要見一個重要的客戶。
column6: Wǒ jīntiān yào jiàn yī ge zhòngyào de kèhù.
column7: I am meeting an important client today.
column9: A business client or account: 重要客戶, 客戶服務, 接待客戶. A shopper in a store is 顧客. A client program or app is 客戶端.

column3: Buy one with 买彩票, win with 中彩票 or 中奖; the ticket takes 张. On the mainland one state lottery is called 福利彩票. Taiwan says 彩券.
column6: Tā mǎi le yī zhāng cǎipiào.
column7: He bought a lottery ticket.
column9: Buy one with 買彩票, win with 中彩票 or 中獎; the ticket takes 張. On the mainland one state lottery is called 福利彩票. Taiwan says 彩券.

column3: The money in a bank, or the act of putting it there: 银行存款, 定期存款 (time deposit). For the everyday act, 存钱 is plainer, and withdrawing is 取款.
column6: Wǒ de cúnkuǎn bù duō.
column7: I do not have much in savings.
column9: The money in a bank, or the act of putting it there: 銀行存款, 定期存款 (time deposit). For the everyday act, 存錢 is plainer, and withdrawing is 取款.

column3: Used with banks and institutions, from either side: 向银行贷款 is borrowing, and 银行贷款给他 is lending. A mortgage is 房贷. Between friends use 借钱.
column4: 他向银行贷款买了房子。
column5: 他向銀行貸款買了房子。
column6: Tā xiàng yínháng dàikuǎn mǎi le fángzi.
column7: He took out a bank loan to buy a house.
column9: Used with banks and institutions, from either side: 向銀行貸款 is borrowing, and 銀行貸款給他 is lending. A mortgage is 房貸. Between friends use 借錢.

column3: Also lacking, in set phrases: 欠考虑, 欠佳. A common sign of an unpaid bill is 欠费: 手机欠费了. It began as a kneeling person with an open mouth, the same part in 次, 吹 and 歌.
column6: Tā hái qiàn wǒ yībǎi kuài qián.
column7: He still owes me a hundred yuan.
column9: Also lacking, in set phrases: 欠考慮, 欠佳. A common sign of an unpaid bill is 欠費: 手機欠費了. It began as a kneeling person with an open mouth, the same part in 次, 吹 and 歌.

column3: Three everyday uses: lose money in business (赔钱, opposite 赚钱), pay for damage (我赔你一个), and 赔不是 to apologize.
column6: Tā zuò shēngyi péi le hěn duō qián.
column7: He lost a lot of money in business.
column9: Three everyday uses: lose money in business (賠錢, opposite 賺錢), pay for damage (我賠你一個), and 賠不是 to apologize.

column3: Formal, used in law, contracts and accidents: 赔偿损失, 要求赔偿, 赔偿金. The payer is liable for the loss, as against 补偿, a making-up without liability. In small everyday cases people say 赔.
column4: 保险公司赔偿了他的损失。
column5: 保險公司賠償了他的損失。
column6: Bǎoxiǎn gōngsī péicháng le tā de sǔnshī.
column7: The insurance company compensated him for his loss.
column9: Formal, used in law, contracts and accidents: 賠償損失, 要求賠償, 賠償金. The payer is liable for the loss, as against 補償, a making-up without liability. In small everyday cases people say 賠.

column3: Making up for a loss with money, time or something else: 经济补偿, 补偿损失. Unlike 赔偿, the payer need not be at fault: an employer or a government can pay it. 补 goes back to a word for patching and mending.
column6: Gōngsī gěi le tā yī bǐ bǔcháng.
column7: The company gave him a sum as compensation.
column9: Making up for a loss with money, time or something else: 經濟補償, 補償損失. Unlike 賠償, the payer need not be at fault: an employer or a government can pay it. 補 goes back to a word for patching and mending.

column3: Money from a government or employer to cover a cost: 交通补贴, 住房补贴. 贴 here is to make up money, as in 贴钱; a person can also 补贴家用.
column6: Zhèngfǔ gěi nóngmín fā bǔtiē.
column7: The government pays subsidies to farmers.
column9: Money from a government or employer to cover a cost: 交通補貼, 住房補貼. 貼 here is to make up money, as in 貼錢; a person can also 補貼家用.

column3: Earning by your own work: 挣钱, 挣工资. 挣钱 is northern speech; 赚钱 is used everywhere.
column6: Tā yī ge yuè zhèng wǔqiān kuài qián.
column7: He earns five thousand yuan a month.
